classes.qualifier-missing-from-name: the definition adds an identifying attribute the name lacks (normalisation, a vector or component where the name states a scalar, an ion-only population where the name states an element, a reference-relative value, an equivalent-electron count, an averaged form, extra weighting), so the name alone denotes a broader or different quantity
classes.definition-narrower-than-name: the definition restricts applicability to a subset of the objects the name covers (a coil family, an instrument, a plasma regime or surface, a layer)
classes.abstract-parent-as-quantity: the definition declares a parent, umbrella or structural quantity whose population, component, averaging or specialised forms are fixed by more specific instances
classes.unit-does-not-fit-name: the unit's physical dimension contradicts the quantity the name states
classes.agrees: the definition states the same scope the name states

items.name: implicit_electron_energy_source_rate
items.description: Implicit electron energy source rate is the signed coefficient whose product with the energy equation's primary quantity gives the implicitly treated electron energy source or sink.
items.documentation:
Implicit electron energy source rate is the multiplicative coefficient of the implicitly treated part of a decomposed electron energy source term. It specifies a source or sink contribution proportional to the primary quantity of the electron energy transport equation.

The source decomposition is:

$$
F_{e,W} = F_{e,W}^{\mathrm{exp}} + S_{e,W}^{\mathrm{imp}} u_e
$$

where $F_{e,W}$ is the complete source term in the chosen electron energy equation, $F_{e,W}^{\mathrm{exp}}$ is its additive explicit contribution, $S_{e,W}^{\mathrm{imp}}$ is the implicit electron energy source rate, and $u_e$ is the equation's primary quantity. The subscripts $e$ and $W$ identify the electron population and energy channel. In a temperature-based formulation, $u_e$ is electron temperature; all source terms must correspond to that same formulation.

This coefficient applies to the electron energy channel and is neither the additive explicit source nor the complete source term. It has the same decomposition role as the [implicit ion energy source rate](name:implicit_ion_energy_source_rate), but applies to electrons rather than ions. Unlike the [implicit electron particle source rate](name:implicit_electron_particle_source_rate), which multiplies electron number density in particle balance, it multiplies the primary quantity of the energy equation.

Sign convention: Positive when multiplication by a positive primary quantity gives an energy gain for electrons; negative when it gives an energy loss.

items.name: current_of_passive_structure
items.description: Current in a passive structure is the signed rate of conventional charge transport circulating toroidally through one axisymmetric member.
items.documentation:
Current of passive structure

The current $I$ is defined by

$$
I = \int_S \mathbf{J}\cdot\hat{\phi}\,dS
$$

where $S$ is the member's full poloidal cross-section, $\mathbf{J}$ is the [conventional electric current density](name:current_density), and $dS$ is a surface-area element. The vector $\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

This quantity integrates current density over one member's cross-section; it is not a sum over all passive structures and excludes plasma and active-coil currents. When the specified member is a passive loop, it equals the [current of that loop](name:current_of_passive_loop).

Sign convention: Positive when conventional electric current flows in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: vertical_coordinate_of_conductor_cross_section
items.description: Vertical coordinate of the geometric center of a rectangular conductor cross-section in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
Vertical coordinate of the geometric center of a rectangular conductor cross-section in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical position.

The coordinate is defined by

$$
Z = \mathbf{x}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{z}}
$$

where $\mathbf{x}$ is the position vector of the geometric center relative to an origin on the toroidal symmetry axis in the chosen zero-height plane, and $\hat{\mathbf{z}}$ is the unit vector along that axis toward increasing vertical position.

This is the [vertical coordinate of the rectangle center](name:vertical_coordinate_of_rectangle_center) applied to a conductor cross-section. It locates one cross-section center, not an average over conductor elements, the rectangle's vertical extent, or an outline vertex.

Sign convention: Positive when the geometric center lies above the zero-height plane in the direction of increasing $Z$.

items.name: power_of_breeder_blanket_module
items.description: Power quantity associated with a single breeder blanket module, abstracting over incident neutron surface loads, volumetric nuclear energy deposition, plasma radiation, and total thermal output as distinct energy-budget components.
items.documentation:
A breeder blanket module participates in multiple distinct energy-exchange pathways between the fusion plasma and the blanket structure. The principal power channels resolved at the module level include the neutron surface load characterized by [incident_power_of_breeder_blanket_module](name:incident_neutron_power_of_breeder_blanket_module), the volumetric nuclear energy deposited inside the module through scattering and capture reactions described by neutron_power_of_breeder_blanket_module, and the electromagnetic photon flux from plasma bremsstrahlung and line radiation quantified by [radiated_power_of_breeder_blanket_module](name:radiated_power_of_breeder_blanket_module).

The total power delivered to the module coolant combines these channels:

$$
P_\mathrm{module} = P_n + P_\mathrm{rad,abs} + P_\mathrm{aux}
$$

where $P_n$ is the deposited neutron power, $P_\mathrm{rad,abs}$ is the absorbed fraction of incident plasma radiation after surface reflection, and $P_\mathrm{aux}$ covers auxiliary heating contributions; nuclear multiplication reactions in the tritium-breeding material can amplify $P_n$ above the incident neutron surface load.

Module-level power quantities are computed from neutronics transport simulations for nuclear deposition channels, coupled with plasma radiation models for photon loads, and validated against calorimetric measurements of coolant enthalpy rise, the latter captured by [net_thermal_power_of_breeder_blanket_module](name:net_thermal_power_of_breeder_blanket_module). The blanket-wide integral summed over all modules is given by [nuclear_heating_power_of_breeder_blanket](name:nuclear_heating_power_of_breeder_blanket).

items.name: parallel_ion_charge_state_energy_flux
items.description: Parallel ion charge-state energy flux is the signed conductive and convective energy transported along the local magnetic field per unit perpendicular area and time for one ion species and charge state.
items.documentation:
Parallel ion charge-state energy flux is the net conductive and convective energy transport along the local magnetic field, measured per unit area perpendicular to that field and per unit time.

The field-aligned projection is defined by:

$$
\Gamma_{\parallel} = \boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{W}\cdot\frac{\mathbf{B}}{|\mathbf{B}|}
$$

where $\Gamma_{\parallel}$ is the signed parallel energy flux, $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{W}$ is the [ion charge-state energy-flux vector](name:ion_charge_state_energy_flux) for the selected species and charge state, $\mathbf{B}$ is the local magnetic field, and $|\mathbf{B}|$ is its magnitude. The subscript $W$ identifies the energy transport channel.

This local quantity applies to one ion species in one specified charge state, without summing over species or charge states. Its edge-plasma scope includes the scrape-off layer and divertor. It excludes perpendicular energy transport and is not restricted to the conductive contribution alone.

It is the parallel component of the parent energy flux, not its magnitude or a surface-integrated power. Unlike the [parallel ion charge-state particle flux](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_particle_flux), it represents transported energy rather than transported particle number.

Sign convention: Positive when net energy transport by the specified ion charge state is in the direction of the local magnetic field.

items.name: fast_neutron_flux_of_toroidal_field_coil
items.description: Incident crossing rate of fast neutrons per unit area on the inboard-facing surface of a toroidal field coil.
items.documentation:
Incident crossing rate of fast neutrons per unit area on the inboard-facing surface of a toroidal field coil is the surface density of neutrons whose kinetic energy is at or above the fast-neutron threshold and whose trajectories cross that surface into the coil. The inboard-facing surface is the side of the toroidal field coil facing the toroidal symmetry axis.

At a point on that surface, the defining angular-flux integral is:

$$
\Phi_\mathrm{fast}^{\mathrm{TF,in}}(\mathbf{x}) = \int_{E_\mathrm{fast}}^\infty \int_{4\pi} \varphi_n(\mathbf{x}, E, \hat{\Omega})\, \max\!\left(0, -\hat{\Omega}\!\cdot\!\hat{\mathbf{n}}_\mathrm{TF,in}(\mathbf{x})\right)\, d\Omega\, dE
$$

where $\Phi_\mathrm{fast}^{\mathrm{TF,in}}$ is the fast neutron flux of the toroidal field coil at surface point $\mathbf{x}$, $\mathbf{x}$ is a point on the inboard-facing surface, $E$ is neutron kinetic energy, $E_\mathrm{fast}$ is the fast-neutron threshold, $\hat{\Omega}$ is neutron flight direction, $\varphi_n$ is the angular neutron flux, $\hat{\mathbf{n}}_\mathrm{TF,in}$ is the unit normal directed outward from the coil material at the inboard-facing surface, and $d\Omega$ is the solid-angle element.

The scope is limited to toroidal field coils and to their inboard-facing surfaces; it does not include correction coils, poloidal field coils, the outboard-facing surface, or a whole-coil combination of surfaces. The quantity is normalized by the receiving surface area and is not the area-integrated neutron rate, cumulative neutron fluence, total neutron production rate, or material response caused by the neutron field.

The fast-neutron threshold is an essential part of the convention: neutrons below $E_\mathrm{fast}$ are excluded, and a different threshold defines a different fast-neutron flux. The analogous quantity for a correction coil is [fast neutron flux of correction coil](name:fast_neutron_flux_of_correction_coil); it uses the same incident fast-neutron crossing concept but a different coil population.

items.name: carbon_prefill_count_due_to_gas_injection
items.description: Cumulative equivalent-electron inventory introduced as carbon gas during plasma prefill, with six count units assigned to each injected carbon atom.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the cumulative equivalent-electron inventory of carbon introduced by gas injection during the plasma prefill phase, before plasma breakdown. It represents injected carbon atoms rather than an instantaneous injection rate.

The defining relation is

$$
N_{\mathrm{C,eq}} = Z_{\mathrm{C}}N_{\mathrm{C}} = 6N_{\mathrm{C}}
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{C,eq}}$ is the equivalent-electron count, $N_{\mathrm{C}}$ is the cumulative number of injected carbon atoms, and $Z_{\mathrm{C}}=6$ is the carbon atomic number. Both counts are dimensionless.

The prefill interval ends at plasma breakdown, so post-breakdown carbon delivery is represented separately by [accumulated carbon count due to gas injection](name:accumulated_carbon_count_due_to_gas_injection). The aggregation convention parallels [accumulated hydrogen prefill count](name:accumulated_hydrogen_prefill_count), with the atomic number providing the equivalent-electron weighting.

items.name: parallel_neutral_particle_flux
items.description: Parallel neutral particle flux is the signed net number flow of one neutral species along the local magnetic field per unit perpendicular area and time, summed over internal states.
items.documentation:
Parallel neutral particle flux is the local signed net number flow of one neutral atomic or molecular species along the magnetic-field direction, per area perpendicular to that direction. Particle crossings in opposite directions contribute with opposite signs.

The parallel projection is defined by:

$$
\Gamma_{0,\parallel} = \boldsymbol{\Gamma}_0 \cdot \frac{\mathbf{B}}{|\mathbf{B}|}
$$

where $\Gamma_{0,\parallel}$ is the parallel neutral particle flux, $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_0$ is the particle number-flux vector of the selected neutral species, $\mathbf{B}$ is the local magnetic-field vector, and $|\mathbf{B}|$ is its magnitude. The subscript $0$ identifies neutral particles. This projection requires a nonzero magnetic field.

The quantity is summed over all internal states of the selected species, not over different neutral species. The [parallel neutral internal-state particle flux](name:parallel_neutral_internal_state_particle_flux) resolves the individual state contributions whose sum gives this quantity.

This is the specialization of [neutral particle flux](name:neutral_particle_flux) for a crossing surface whose normal follows the local magnetic-field direction. It is not a flux per actual material-surface area at an arbitrary field-incidence angle, a surface-integrated arrival rate, or a one-way incident flux. The magnetic field defines the projection direction without implying that neutral trajectories follow magnetic field lines.

Sign convention: Positive when the net neutral particle transport points along the local magnetic-field vector.

items.name: stray_breakdown_magnetic_field
items.description: Residual magnetic-field strength at the plasma position during initiation, produced by imperfect cancelation of external coil fields and capable of inhibiting electron-avalanche breakdown.
items.documentation:
This quantity denotes the residual magnetic-field contribution present at the plasma position during plasma initiation. It arises when external coil fields are not completely canceled and is relevant because residual field can inhibit the electron avalanche required for breakdown.

It is the stray contribution to the [breakdown magnetic field](name:breakdown_magnetic_field), rather than the complete field describing the initiation state. The associated [stray breakdown magnetic-field magnitude](name:stray_breakdown_magnetic_field_magnitude) provides the Euclidean magnitude when a direction-independent measure is required; this parent quantity does not by itself specify a field direction.

items.name: toroidal_fast_particle_torque_due_to_j_cross_b_force
items.description: Volume-integrated toroidal angular-momentum transfer to fast particles from the Lorentz force associated with their radial current.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the total toroidal torque transferred to the fast-particle population by the electromagnetic force associated with its radial current, integrated over the plasma volume.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, with $\hat{R}\times\hat{\phi}=\hat{Z}$, the radial-current contribution is defined by

$$
\mathcal{T}_{\phi}=\int_V -R\,j_{R}^{\mathrm{fast}} B_Z\,\mathrm{d}V
$$

where $\mathcal{T}_{\phi}$ is the toroidal torque, $R$ is major radius, $j_{R}^{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the radial current density carried by fast particles, $B_Z$ is the vertical magnetic-field component, and $V$ is the plasma volume. Equivalently, the integrand is $R(\mathbf{j}^{\mathrm{fast}}\times\mathbf{B})_\phi$ when restricted to the radial-current contribution.

This is a volume-integrated quantity and is distinct from the local [toroidal torque density due to the j-cross-B force](name:toroidal_torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force) and from collisional torque transfer to fast particles [toroidal fast torque due to collisions](name:toroidal_fast_torque_due_to_collisions).

Sign convention: Positive when the resulting torque points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: accumulated_lithium_prefill_count_due_to_gas_injection
items.description: Cumulative equivalent-electron inventory of lithium introduced by gas injection during plasma prefill, assigning three count units to each lithium atom.
items.documentation:
The accumulated lithium prefill count is the equivalent-electron inventory of lithium introduced by gas injection before plasma breakdown. Each lithium atom contributes three equivalent-electron counts, corresponding to its atomic number.

The defining accumulation is

$$
N_{\mathrm{eq,Li}} = Z_{\mathrm{Li}} N_{\mathrm{Li}} = 3\int_{t_{\mathrm{start}}}^{t_{\mathrm{bd}}} \dot{N}_{\mathrm{Li}}(t)\,dt
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{eq,Li}}$ is the equivalent-electron inventory, $Z_{\mathrm{Li}}$ is lithium's atomic number, $N_{\mathrm{Li}}$ is the introduced lithium-atom inventory, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Li}}$ is the lithium injection rate, $t_{\mathrm{start}}$ is the prefill start time, and $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ is the plasma-breakdown time.

This quantity describes delivered lithium inventory during prefill, not the instantaneous [lithium source rate](name:lithium_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection), post-breakdown [accumulated lithium count](name:accumulated_lithium_count_due_to_gas_injection), or the inventory of all injected species represented by [accumulated total prefill gas count](name:accumulated_total_prefill_gas_count).

items.name: accumulated_xenon_prefill_count
items.description: Cumulative equivalent-electron inventory of neutral xenon introduced during plasma prefill, ending at plasma breakdown, with 54 count units per atom.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the equivalent-electron inventory of neutral xenon gas introduced between the start of prefill and plasma breakdown. It represents the accumulated prefill contribution, not an instantaneous injection rate.

The defining accumulation is

$$
N_{\mathrm{Xe,eq}}^{\mathrm{prefill}} = Z_{\mathrm{Xe}} \int_{t_0}^{t_{\mathrm{bd}}} \dot{N}_{\mathrm{Xe}}(t)\,dt
$$

where $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Xe}}(t)$ is the neutral xenon atom injection rate, $t_0$ and $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ are the prefill start and breakdown times, and $Z_{\mathrm{Xe}}=54$ is xenon's atomic number. The resulting count assigns 54 equivalent-electron units to each xenon atom.

This quantity is the prefill component of xenon_prefill_count and excludes xenon introduced after breakdown, which is represented by accumulated_xenon_count.

items.name: toroidal_argon_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier
items.description: Signed toroidal bulk-flow velocity of argon ions, density-weighted over charge states and evaluated at the radial location of an internal transport barrier.
items.documentation:
The quantity is the density-weighted mean bulk-flow velocity of all argon ion charge states at the radial location assigned to the internal transport barrier. Neutral argon is excluded, and the value is not a volume average over the barrier or surrounding plasma.

For argon charge states indexed by $q$, the velocity is defined by

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{Ar}} = \frac{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{Ar}^{q+}} v_{\phi,\mathrm{Ar}^{q+}}}{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{Ar}^{q+}}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Ar}^{q+}}$ is the number density of charge state $q$ and $v_{\phi,\mathrm{Ar}^{q+}}$ is its bulk-flow component along the toroidal unit vector. The toroidal direction is defined in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, with $\phi$ increasing toroidally. The charge-state aggregation is the same as for [toroidal_carbon_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier](name:toroidal_carbon_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier).

Sign convention: Positive when the argon-ion bulk flow points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: volume_averaged_ion_density
items.description: Number density of ions of a specified species, summed over all ionic charge states and averaged over the confined plasma volume inside the last closed flux surface.
items.documentation:
Number density of ion

The volume average of the local [ion density](name:ion_density) is defined by

$$
\langle n_i\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V}\int_V n_i\,dV
$$

where $i$ labels the specified ion species, $n_i$ is its local ion number density, $\langle n_i\rangle_V$ is its volume-averaged number density, $V$ is the confined plasma volume enclosed by the last closed flux surface, and $dV$ is a volume element.

The species density is summed over all ionic charge states and includes thermal and nonthermal ions; neutral particles are excluded. This is a single-species particle number density, not an all-species total, electric charge density, or mass density. It is a volume mean rather than a local value or a chord mean.

Multiplying this average by the confined plasma volume gives the total number of ions of the specified species within that volume. The [volume-averaged argon density](name:volume_averaged_argon_density) is a species-specific instance of the same averaging definition.

items.name: accumulated_argon_count
items.description: Accumulated argon count is the cumulative equivalent-electron inventory of argon atoms delivered by gas injection after plasma breakdown. Each argon atom contributes 18 equivalent electrons, equal to its atomic number; this is delivered inventory, not plasma electron content or ionization state.
items.documentation:
Accumulated argon count is the cumulative equivalent-electron inventory of argon atoms delivered by gas injection after plasma breakdown. Each delivered argon atom contributes $Z_{\mathrm{Ar}}=18$ equivalent electrons, equal to the atomic number of argon.

The accumulated count is defined by integrating the delivered argon atom injection rate from the plasma-breakdown time:

$$
N_{\mathrm{Ar,eq}}(t) = Z_{\mathrm{Ar}} \int_{t_{\mathrm{bd}}}^{t} \dot{N}_{\mathrm{Ar}}(t')\,dt', \qquad Z_{\mathrm{Ar}} = 18
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{Ar,eq}}$ is the dimensionless equivalent-electron argon count, $Z_{\mathrm{Ar}}$ is the dimensionless atomic number of argon, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Ar}}$ is the argon atom injection rate in atoms per second, $t$ is time in seconds, and $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ is the plasma-breakdown time in seconds.

This quantity includes only argon delivered after breakdown. Argon introduced before breakdown belongs to the pre-breakdown inventory represented by argon_count; the accumulated value is not a measure of free electrons, plasma argon content, retained argon, or argon ionization state, and is not reduced by subsequent pumping, exhaust, wall retention, ionization, radiation, or redistribution.

items.name: z_direction_unit_vector_of_pellet_injector
items.description: Z component of the unit vector aligned with the unshattered pellet velocity immediately before shattering, resolved in the right-handed Cartesian (x, y, z) frame.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the signed projection of the unshattered pellet-injection direction onto the Cartesian z axis immediately before shattering. It describes orientation only, not the pellet speed or the velocity of shattered fragments.

The component is defined by:

$$
d_z = \hat{\mathbf{d}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{z}}
$$

where $\hat{\mathbf{d}}$ is the unit vector aligned with the unshattered pellet velocity and $\hat{\mathbf{z}}$ is the unit vector along increasing z in the right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$ frame. Together with the corresponding [x component](name:x_unit_vector_of_pellet_injector) and [y component](name:y_unit_vector_of_pellet_injector), it specifies the injection direction.

items.name: argon_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection
items.description: Instantaneous equivalent-electron argon source rate delivered to the plasma vessel by gas injection systems, where each injected argon atom with Z = 18 contributes 18 equivalent-electron counts.
items.documentation:
The argon source rate due to gas injection characterizes the instantaneous rate at which neutral argon with atomic number $Z_{\mathrm{Ar}} = 18$ is admitted to the plasma vessel by gas injection hardware, expressed as an equivalent-electron count rate. The equivalent-electron convention counts each injected neutral argon atom as 18 equivalent electrons because neutral argon has 18 electrons; this is an inventory-accounting convention, not a statement about subsequent ionization or confinement.

The defining relation for injected argon is:

$$
\dot{S}_{\mathrm{Ar}} = Z_{\mathrm{Ar}}\,\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Ar}} = 18\,\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Ar}}
$$

where $\dot{S}_{\mathrm{Ar}}$ is the argon equivalent-electron source rate, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Ar}}$ is the raw argon-atom delivery rate in atoms per second, and $Z_{\mathrm{Ar}} = 18$ is the dimensionless atomic number of argon.

This quantity is the argon-species member of [source_rate_due_to_gas_injection](name:source_rate_due_to_gas_injection). It is the instantaneous time derivative of the corresponding accumulated equivalent-electron inventory [accumulated_argon_count](name:accumulated_argon_count), and differs from raw gas-particle source rates by the factor $Z_{\mathrm{Ar}}$.

Sign convention: Positive when argon is delivered into the plasma vessel, increasing the equivalent-electron particle inventory.

items.name: carbon_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection
items.description: Instantaneous equivalent-electron carbon source rate delivered to the plasma vessel by gas injection systems, with each injected carbon atom contributing six equivalent-electron counts.
items.documentation:
The carbon source rate due to gas injection characterizes the instantaneous rate at which neutral carbon with atomic number six is admitted to the plasma vessel by gas injection, expressed as an equivalent-electron count rate. It is the carbon-specific component of [source rate due to gas injection](name:source_rate_due_to_gas_injection).

For carbon injection, the defining relation is:

$$
\dot{S}_{\mathrm{C}} = 6\,\dot{N}_{\mathrm{C}}
$$

where $\dot{S}_{\mathrm{C}}$ is the equivalent-electron source rate and $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{C}}$ is the raw carbon-atom delivery rate; both rates have units of inverse seconds.

This quantity counts injected carbon atoms, not electrons currently present in the plasma, carbon ionization states, or the net carbon balance after transport and removal. Its time integral gives [accumulated carbon count due to gas injection](name:accumulated_carbon_count_due_to_gas_injection). The same equivalent-electron convention applies to [tritium source rate due to gas injection](name:tritium_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection), with a different atomic-number factor.

Sign convention: Positive when carbon gas is delivered into the vessel, increasing the equivalent-electron inventory.

items.name: length_of_pellet
items.description: End-to-end extent of an intact cylindrical pellet measured along its symmetry axis before injection or shattering.
items.documentation:
The pellet axial length is the distance between the two end faces measured parallel to the symmetry axis of the intact cylindrical pellet.

$$
L_p = z_2 - z_1
$$

where $L_p$ is the axial length and $z_1$ and $z_2$ are the axial coordinates of the two end faces, ordered so that $z_2 > z_1$ along the chosen axial direction.

This quantity describes the unshattered pellet before injection or fragmentation and excludes its transverse size, which is described by the [diameter of the pellet](name:diameter_of_pellet).

items.name: wave_phase_of_antenna_strap
items.description: Phase angle of the radio-frequency current phasor carried by one ion-cyclotron-heating antenna strap, defined relative to a specified RF phase reference.
items.documentation:
Wave phase of an antenna strap is the phase angle of the oscillatory radio-frequency current phasor carried by that strap. It describes the strap-level excitation phase used in the antenna's toroidal phasing configuration.

The complex strap-current phasor may be represented as

$$
I_s = |I_s|e^{i\phi_s}
$$

where $I_s$ is the complex radio-frequency current phasor, $|I_s|$ is its current amplitude, and $\phi_s$ is the wave phase represented by this quantity. The phase is defined modulo $2\pi$ relative to a specified RF reference phase.

This quantity applies to one antenna strap and is not summed or averaged over multiple straps. It refers to the phase of the strap current, not the phase of a forward power-wave phasor, which is represented by [forward wave phase of an ion-cyclotron-heating antenna](name:forward_wave_phase_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna), or the phase associated with a complete antenna element.

The associated [wave current of antenna strap](name:wave_current_of_antenna_strap) provides the phasor whose phase is specified, while wave current of antenna strap amplitude determines its magnitude rather than its phase. Relative phases between straps determine the toroidal phasing of the antenna excitation and therefore influence the launched wave excitation spectrum. The phase-reference plane and any phase-unwrapping convention must be specified separately when comparing values.

items.name: tritium_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection
items.description: Instantaneous equivalent-electron tritium source rate delivered to the plasma vessel by gas injection, with each injected tritium atom contributing one equivalent-electron count.
items.documentation:
The tritium source rate due to gas injection characterizes the instantaneous rate at which neutral tritium with atomic number $Z_{\mathrm{T}} = 1$ is admitted to the plasma vessel by gas injection hardware, expressed as an equivalent-electron count rate. It is the tritium-specific component of the [source rate due to gas injection](name:source_rate_due_to_gas_injection).

The defining relation is:

$$
\dot{S}_{\mathrm{T}} = Z_{\mathrm{T}} \dot{N}_{\mathrm{T}} = \dot{N}_{\mathrm{T}}
$$

where $\dot{S}_{\mathrm{T}}$ is the equivalent-electron source rate, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{T}}$ is the raw tritium atom delivery rate in atoms per second, and $Z_{\mathrm{T}}$ is tritium's atomic number. The rate is the instantaneous derivative of the accumulated inventory [accumulated tritium count due to gas injection](name:accumulated_tritium_count_due_to_gas_injection), and it counts delivered atoms rather than plasma electron content or ionization state.

Sign convention: Positive when tritium gas is being delivered into the vessel, increasing the equivalent-electron inventory.

items.name: height_of_hard_xray_detector
items.description: Height of a hard X-ray detector is the full edge-to-edge extent of its rectangular aperture along the second local tangential axis, X2, in the local Cartesian (X1, X2, X3) frame.
items.documentation:
Height of hard xray detector

It applies to a rectangular detector aperture and denotes a full extent, not a half-extent, signed coordinate, detector location, housing dimension, or extent along the local normal. It is distinct from the extent of a separate channel collimating aperture and from the first local tangential extent, represented by the [first local tangential width](name:first_local_tangential_width_of_hard_xray_detector).

For a rectangular detector aperture, this height and the [first local tangential width](name:first_local_tangential_width_of_hard_xray_detector) are its two orthogonal in-plane full dimensions; together they determine the aperture opening area. That area contributes to the [hard X-ray detector etendue](name:etendue_of_hard_xray_detector), which also depends on the accepted solid angle.

items.name: first_local_tangential_width_of_neutron_detector
items.description: Full transverse extent of the rectangular collimating aperture associated with a neutron detector, measured between its edges along the aperture’s first local tangential direction.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the full transverse width of the neutron detector’s collimating aperture along its first local tangential direction. It describes the aperture opening rather than the external detector body, housing, or shielding.

The width is defined by

$$
w_1 = x_{1,\max} - x_{1,\min}
$$

where $w_1$ is the first local tangential aperture width, and $x_{1,\max}$ and $x_{1,\min}$ are the positions of the two aperture edges along the first local tangential axis.

This quantity applies only to a rectangular aperture and represents the complete edge-to-edge opening dimension, not a radius or half-width. The other transverse dimension is represented by the second local tangential width of the neutron detector, whereas a circular opening is characterized by the [radius of the neutron detector](name:radius_of_neutron_detector) rather than by rectangular widths.

items.name: neutral_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination
items.description: Outgoing neutral-particle number flux density from recombination at a plasma-facing wall, summed over emitted neutral species and internal states.
items.documentation:
Recombination-associated neutral particle flux at a plasma-facing wall is the rate per unit wall area at which neutral products leave the surface and enter the adjacent plasma. It counts particles rather than the energy or momentum they carry.

The flux is defined by

$$
\Gamma_{\mathrm{rec}}^{\mathrm{out}} = \frac{dN_{\mathrm{rec}}^{\mathrm{out}}}{dA\,dt}
$$

where $\Gamma_{\mathrm{rec}}^{\mathrm{out}}$ is the outgoing recombination-associated neutral particle-number flux density, $N_{\mathrm{rec}}^{\mathrm{out}}$ is the corresponding number of emitted neutral particles, $A$ is plasma-facing wall area, and $t$ is time.

The quantity applies to neutral products generated when incident plasma ions recombine or neutralize at the wall. It is summed over contributing incident-ion species and charge states, recombination channels, emitted neutral species, and emitted internal states. It excludes energy weighting and therefore differs from [energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination](name:energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination).

This neutral emitted-particle quantity is the neutral-product specialization of particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination. It is distinct from [incident_neutral_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination](name:incident_neutral_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination), which counts recombination-associated neutral particles arriving at the wall, and from [neutral_internal_state_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination](name:neutral_internal_state_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination), which resolves the emitted flux by internal state.

Sign convention: Positive when neutral particles travel from the plasma-facing wall into the adjacent plasma.

items.name: radial_momentum_flux
items.description: Rate of transport of radial linear momentum per unit area across an oriented surface in the plasma, combining convective, isotropic-pressure, and viscous or turbulent-stress contributions, with radial defined along increasing major radius in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
The radial momentum flux is the radial component of the linear-momentum flux crossing an oriented surface in the plasma. It includes convective transport together with isotropic pressure and viscous or turbulent stress contributions projected onto the $\hat{R}$ direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius measured from the toroidal symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle increasing counter-clockwise when viewed from above $+\hat{Z}$, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The radial projection of the momentum current through an oriented surface is:

$$
\Gamma_{\Pi,R} = \hat{R}\cdot\boldsymbol{\Pi}\cdot\hat{n}
$$

where $\Gamma_{\Pi,R}$ is this radial momentum flux, $\hat{R}$ is the radial basis vector of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, $\boldsymbol{\Pi}$ is the tensor associated with [momentum flux](name:momentum_flux), and $\hat{n}$ is the chosen unit normal of the oriented surface. For a single plasma fluid, $\boldsymbol{\Pi}$ contains the convective term $\rho\mathbf{v}\mathbf{v}$, scalar-pressure term $p\mathbf{I}$, and viscous or turbulent stress term $\boldsymbol{\pi}$, where $\rho$ is mass density, $\mathbf{v}$ is bulk flow velocity, $p$ is scalar pressure, $\mathbf{I}$ is the identity tensor, and $\boldsymbol{\pi}$ is the viscous or turbulent stress tensor.

This name denotes the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ radial projection of the momentum current, not a flux-surface-normal projection and not a derivative with respect to a radial flux label. It is the radial direction-resolved form of [momentum flux](name:momentum_flux), distinct from other direction-resolved or population-resolved momentum-flux quantities.

Sign convention: Positive when the momentum current through the oriented surface has a component in the direction of increasing major radius $R$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: fast_ion_power_due_to_collisions
items.description: Volume-integrated Coulomb collisional power transferred to the total fast-ion population by background ions, summed over all fast-ion species and charge states.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the volume-integrated net rate of energy transfer into the complete fast-ion population from Coulomb scattering interactions with background ions. It aggregates all fast-ion species and charge states without resolving the receiving fast-ion subpopulation.

The volume-integrated fast-ion collisional power is defined as:

$$
P_{\mathrm{fast\text{-}ion,coll}} = \int_V Q_{\mathrm{fast\text{-}ion,coll}}(\mathbf{r})\,dV
$$

where $Q_{\mathrm{fast\text{-}ion,coll}}$ is the local collisional power-exchange density into the aggregate fast-ion population, $\mathbf{r}$ is position, $dV$ is the differential volume element, and $V$ is the plasma volume.

This quantity is the fast-ion component of [ion power due to collisions](name:ion_power_due_to_collisions). Its charge-state-resolved counterpart is [fast ion charge state power due to collisions](name:fast_ion_charge_state_power_due_to_collisions), while [thermal ion power due to collisions](name:thermal_ion_power_due_to_collisions) describes transfer into thermal ions. Internal exchanges among fast-ion species cancel in the summed net value.

Sign convention: Positive when Coulomb scattering interactions transfer net energy into the complete fast-ion population.

items.name: nitrogen_prefill_count
items.description: Nitrogen prefill count is the total amount of neutral nitrogen (N or N₂) introduced before plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count with 7 per atom or 14 per N₂ molecule.
items.documentation:
Nitrogen prefill count is the total amount of neutral nitrogen (N or N₂) introduced during the prefill phase before plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count. Each neutral nitrogen atom contributes 7 equivalent electrons, so each N₂ molecule contributes 14.

The equivalent-electron count is defined by

$$
N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{N,prefill}} = 7N_{\mathrm{N,prefill}} + 14N_{\mathrm{N_2,prefill}} = \int_{t_0}^{t_{\mathrm{bd}}} \left[7\dot{N}_{\mathrm{N}}(t) + 14\dot{N}_{\mathrm{N_2}}(t)\right]dt
$$

where $N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{N,prefill}}$ is the equivalent-electron count, $N_{\mathrm{N,prefill}}$ and $N_{\mathrm{N_2,prefill}}$ are accumulated neutral atom and molecule counts, and $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{N}}$ and $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{N_2}}$ are their introduction rates. The counts are pure counts, the rates are in s$^{-1}$, and $t_0$ and $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ are the prefill start and plasma-breakdown times in seconds.

This quantity includes only neutral nitrogen introduced before breakdown and excludes wall recycling, neutral-beam or pellet fueling, later gas injection, and retained or ionized inventory. It is the nitrogen component of [prefill_count](name:prefill_count), whereas accumulated_nitrogen_count represents post-breakdown nitrogen accumulation.

items.name: suprathermal_neutral_internal_state_pressure
items.description: Kinetic pressure contributed by suprathermal neutral particles occupying a specified internal quantum or excitation state, including anisotropic velocity-space contributions from the nonthermal population.
items.documentation:
Suprathermal neutral internal-state pressure is the state-resolved anisotropic kinetic pressure of suprathermal neutral atoms or molecules occupying a specified internal quantum or excitation state. It is a partial pressure for the selected internal state and suprathermal population, not a sum over all internal states and not the thermal neutral contribution.

For state $a$, the pressure tensor of the suprathermal population is the central second velocity-space moment:

$$
\mathbf{P}^{\mathrm{sup}}_a = m_a \int (\mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u}^{\mathrm{sup}}_a) \otimes (\mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u}^{\mathrm{sup}}_a) f^{\mathrm{sup}}_a(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $m_a$ is the particle mass, $f^{\mathrm{sup}}_a(\mathbf{v})$ is the velocity distribution of suprathermal neutrals in state $a$, $\mathbf{u}^{\mathrm{sup}}_a$ is the mean velocity of that selected population, and $\otimes$ denotes the dyadic product. The central moment excludes dynamic pressure from directed bulk flow.

Directional or gyrotropic components are projections or averages of this tensor; for example, [perpendicular suprathermal neutral internal-state pressure](name:perpendicular_suprathermal_neutral_internal_state_pressure) is the component transverse to the local magnetic field. [Thermal neutral internal-state pressure](name:thermal_neutral_internal_state_pressure) is the corresponding thermal contribution, while [total neutral internal-state pressure](name:total_neutral_internal_state_pressure) combines thermal and suprathermal contributions for the same internal state.

items.name: accumulated_ammonia_count
items.description: Cumulative post-breakdown inventory of ammonia molecules introduced into the plasma vessel, expressed as an equivalent-electron count with ten count units assigned to each neutral NH3 molecule.
items.documentation:
The accumulated ammonia count is the cumulative post-breakdown amount of NH3 introduced into the plasma vessel, represented using an equivalent-electron accounting convention. It is the post-breakdown component of the total ammonia count, not a direct count of free plasma electrons.

$$
C_{\mathrm{NH_3}}^{\mathrm{acc}} = (Z_\mathrm{N}+3Z_\mathrm{H})N_{\mathrm{NH_3}}^{\mathrm{acc}} = 10N_{\mathrm{NH_3}}^{\mathrm{acc}}
$$

Here, $C_{\mathrm{NH_3}}^{\mathrm{acc}}$ is the accumulated equivalent-electron count, $N_{\mathrm{NH_3}}^{\mathrm{acc}}$ is the cumulative number of ammonia molecules introduced after plasma breakdown, and $Z_\mathrm{N}=7$ and $Z_\mathrm{H}=1$ are the atomic numbers of nitrogen and hydrogen. The quantity excludes ammonia introduced during prefill, which is represented by [ammonia prefill count](name:ammonia_prefill_count), and does not represent instantaneous injection rate, retained neutral inventory, ionization state, or actual free-electron content.

items.name: per_toroidal_mode_fast_ion_power_density
items.description: Flux-surface-averaged volumetric rate of coherent-wave energy transfer to fast, nonthermal ions of a selected species, summed over ionic charge states and resolved by toroidal Fourier mode.
items.documentation:
Toroidal-mode-resolved fast-ion power density is the flux-surface-averaged rate at which an individual toroidal wave harmonic transfers energy to the nonthermal fast-ion population of a selected species per unit physical volume. It describes direct coherent-wave absorption, not subsequent collisional redistribution of the absorbed energy.

For each toroidal harmonic, the averaged deposition density is defined by

$$
p_{i,\mathrm{f}}(n_\phi) = \left\langle \frac{dE_{i,\mathrm{f}}(n_\phi)}{dt\,dV} \right\rangle_{\mathrm{fs}}
$$

where $p_{i,\mathrm{f}}(n_\phi)$ is the mode-resolved fast-ion power density, $i$ labels the selected ion species, $\mathrm{f}$ identifies its fast population, $n_\phi$ is the integer toroidal Fourier mode number, and $E_{i,\mathrm{f}}(n_\phi)$ is the energy transferred by that harmonic to this population. Here $t$ is time, $V$ is physical volume, and $\langle\cdot\rangle_{\mathrm{fs}}$ denotes averaging over the magnetic flux surface.

The species contribution is summed over all ionic charge states, but not over different ion species or toroidal harmonics. The [charge-state-resolved counterpart](name:per_toroidal_mode_fast_ion_charge_state_power_density) separates the contributions whose sum gives this species-level quantity. Thermal ions and electrons are excluded. The flux-surface average is distinct from the unaveraged local deposition density and is not a volume-integrated power.

Summing over a complete, consistently normalized set of toroidal harmonics recovers the flux-surface-averaged [fast-ion power density](name:fast_ion_power_density). Integrating the averaged density over an enclosed physical volume gives the corresponding [mode-resolved fast-ion absorbed wave power](name:per_toroidal_mode_fast_ion_absorbed_wave_power). Each harmonic contribution is an absorbed power density, not a Fourier amplitude of the deposited-power distribution.

Sign convention: Positive when energy is transferred from the coherent wave to the fast-ion population.

items.name: ion_average_temperature_at_pedestal_top
items.description: Density-weighted kinetic temperature of all ion species and charge states evaluated at the core-side shoulder of the H-mode pedestal.
items.documentation:
Ion average temperature at the pedestal top is the density-weighted kinetic temperature of the combined ion population at the core-side shoulder of the H-mode pedestal. It is the ion-specific component of average temperature at the pedestal top.

$$
T_{i,\mathrm{avg}} = \frac{\sum_s n_s T_s}{\sum_s n_s}
$$

where $T_{i,\mathrm{avg}}$ is the ion average temperature, $n_s$ is the number density of ion species or charge state $s$, and $T_s$ is its kinetic temperature. The sum includes all ion species and charge states in the defined ion population; it is not an electron temperature or a temperature for a single ion species. The weighting denominator is the total ion density represented by total ion density at the pedestal top.

items.name: total_xenon_fraction
items.description: Dimensionless abundance ratio of xenon ion number density, summed over ionization states, to electron number density in the same plasma domain.
items.documentation:
The xenon fraction measures the abundance of charged xenon relative to the electron population in a plasma domain. It is a dimensionless part-to-reference ratio, not a xenon density or an effective charge.

The fraction is defined by:

$$
f_{\mathrm{Xe}} = \frac{n_{\mathrm{Xe}}}{n_e}
$$

where $f_{\mathrm{Xe}}$ is the xenon fraction, $n_{\mathrm{Xe}}$ is the total xenon ion number density summed over all positive ionization states, and $n_e$ is the electron number density.

The numerator and denominator refer to the same plasma domain and use the same spatial aggregation convention. Neutral xenon atoms are excluded, and the quantity is not restricted to an individual xenon ionization state. The specific volume-averaged realization applies the averaging operation to both densities before forming the ratio, as defined by [volume_averaged_total_xenon_fraction](name:volume_averaged_total_xenon_fraction).

The underlying xenon density is the charge-state-summed quantity represented by [xenon_density](name:xenon_density); the fraction differs from it by normalization to the electron density. The corresponding volume-averaged xenon density is [volume_averaged_xenon_density](name:volume_averaged_xenon_density), which supplies the numerator for the volume-averaged realization.

items.name: average_temperature_over_scrape_off_layer
items.description: Averaged kinetic temperature of a specified plasma species over the open-field-line scrape-off layer, with the averaging domain and measure defined by its specialization.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the temperature of a specified plasma species after averaging over a defined domain or path within the scrape-off layer. The scrape-off layer is the open-field-line region outside the last closed magnetic flux surface.

The averaged temperature is defined by

$$
\overline{T}_s = \frac{\int_{\mathcal{D}} T_s\,d\mu}{\int_{\mathcal{D}} d\mu}
$$

where $\overline{T}_s$ is the averaged temperature, $T_s$ is the local temperature of species $s$, $\mathcal{D}$ is the specified scrape-off-layer domain or path, and $d\mu$ is the averaging measure. For [field-line-average temperature over the scrape-off layer](name:field_line_average_temperature_over_scrape_off_layer), $\mathcal{D}$ is an open magnetic field line between its defined upstream and downstream locations and $d\mu$ is the corresponding path measure.

The quantity is species-specific and does not sum temperatures over multiple species or represent a local pointwise temperature. It is an averaged specialization of [temperature over the scrape-off layer](name:temperature_over_scrape_off_layer), while the concrete averaging domain and measure distinguish each child quantity.

items.name: ammonia_deuterated_prefill_count
items.description: Deuterated ammonia prefill count is the total amount of neutral ND3 introduced before plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count with 10 count units per molecule.
items.documentation:
Deuterated ammonia prefill count is the total amount of neutral deuterated ammonia (ND3) introduced during the prefill phase before plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count. Each neutral ND3 molecule contributes ten equivalent electrons: seven from nitrogen and one from each of its three deuterium atoms.

The equivalent-electron count is defined by

$$
N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{ND_3,prefill}} = (Z_{\mathrm{N}} + 3Z_{\mathrm{D}})N_{\mathrm{ND_3,prefill}} = 10\int_{t_0}^{t_{\mathrm{bd}}}\dot{N}_{\mathrm{ND_3}}(t)\,dt
$$

where $Z_{\mathrm{N}}=7$ and $Z_{\mathrm{D}}=1$ are atomic numbers, $N_{\mathrm{ND_3,prefill}}$ is the accumulated molecule count, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{ND_3}}$ is the molecule injection rate, and $t_0$ and $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ are the prefill start and breakdown times.

This quantity includes only ND3 introduced before breakdown and excludes wall recycling, neutral-beam or pellet fueling, later gas injection, and retained or ionized inventory. It is the deuterated-ammonia component of [prefill_count](name:prefill_count), distinct from [ammonia_prefill_count](name:ammonia_prefill_count) and post-breakdown [accumulated_ammonia_deuterated_count](name:accumulated_ammonia_deuterated_count).

items.name: upper_bound_energy_of_detector_pixel
items.description: The upper bound energy of a detector pixel is the maximum photon energy at the high-energy edge of its spectral bandpass in an X-ray crystal spectrometer.
items.documentation:
The upper bound energy of a detector pixel is the maximum photon energy at the high-energy edge of the spectral interval accepted by that pixel in an X-ray crystal spectrometer. It defines the upper endpoint of the pixel-specific photon-energy bandpass.

This quantity applies to one detector pixel and describes its individual spectral acceptance interval; it is not an energy averaged over pixels or over the full spectrometer. It is distinct from the representative [energy of a detector pixel](name:energy_of_detector_pixel), which identifies the central or calibrated spectral-channel energy, and from the [lower bound energy of a detector pixel](name:lower_bound_energy_of_detector_pixel), which defines the lower endpoint of the same interval.

Together, the upper and lower bounds delimit the photon-energy range accepted by each pixel, while the representative pixel energy identifies the spectral-channel assignment within that range.

items.name: plasma_current
items.description: Plasma current is the signed integral of a plasma current-density component over a poloidal cross-section; its global equilibrium value is the net toroidal current.
items.documentation:
Plasma current represents conventional electric charge transport carried by the plasma, integrated over a poloidal cross-section and resolved along a specified direction. Its global equilibrium value is the total toroidal current through the full plasma poloidal cross-section.

The component-resolved current is defined by

$$
I_a(S) = \int_S \mathbf{j}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{e}}_a\,dA
$$

where $I_a(S)$ is the integrated plasma current in direction $a$, $a$ labels the selected component, $S$ is the selected poloidal cross-sectional region, $\mathbf{j}$ is the total plasma [current density](name:current_density), $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_a$ is the local unit vector along that component's positive direction, and $dA$ is an unsigned area element.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, $R$ is distance from the symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. The global plasma current is $I_p=I_\phi(S_p)$, where $I_p$ denotes the total toroidal plasma current, $S_p$ is the full plasma poloidal cross-section, and $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_\phi$ points toward increasing toroidal angle.

The current density includes all charged-particle contributions with their electric-charge signs. The integral is therefore a net conventional current, not a particle flux or a sum of unsigned current magnitudes. Currents carried by external coils and conducting structures are excluded.

The [cumulative plasma current inside a flux surface](name:cumulative_inside_flux_surface_plasma_current) restricts the integration region to the poloidal cross-section enclosed by that surface while retaining the specified current component. For the toroidal component, it equals the global plasma current when its integration region coincides with the full plasma cross-section.

Sign convention: Positive when the integrated conventional-current contribution is along the selected positive component direction; for the global toroidal current, this is increasing $\phi$, counterclockwise when viewed from above along the positive vertical axis.

items.name: energy_confinement_enhancement_factor
items.description: Dimensionless ratio comparing the plasma energy confinement time with the IPB98(y,2) reference scaling prediction.
items.documentation:
The energy confinement enhancement factor is the multiplicative departure of a plasma’s global energy confinement time from the IPB98(y,2) reference scaling prediction. It indicates whether energy is retained longer or shorter than the reference predicts for the corresponding scaling inputs.

The factor is defined by:

$$
h_{98} = \frac{\tau_E}{\tau_{E,\mathrm{IPB98(y,2)}}}
$$

where $h_{98}$ is the energy confinement enhancement factor, $\tau_E$ is the plasma energy confinement time, and $\tau_{E,\mathrm{IPB98(y,2)}}$ is the energy confinement time predicted by the IPB98(y,2) reference scaling.

This is a global plasma quantity: the numerator represents the confinement of the total stored plasma energy relative to the corresponding net energy-loss power, aggregated over the plasma rather than assigned to a local region or individual transport channel. It is not itself an energy confinement time, stored energy, power, or local transport coefficient.

A value of one denotes agreement with the reference scaling; a value greater than one denotes longer confinement, and a value less than one denotes shorter confinement than the reference prediction.

items.name: toroidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_source
items.description: The toroidal component of the area-normalized momentum source for a specified ion charge state represents directional momentum transfer in an edge plasma.
items.documentation:
The toroidal component of the area-normalized momentum source for a specified ion charge state represents directional momentum transfer in an edge plasma. It is resolved for one ion species and charge state rather than summed over charge states.

The toroidal component is defined by

$$
S_{\phi,i,q} = \mathbf{S}_{i,q} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $\mathbf{S}_{i,q}$ is the area-normalized momentum source for ion species $i$ in charge state $q$, and $\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

This quantity is the toroidal specialization of the charge-state-resolved vector [ion charge state momentum source](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_source). It represents net momentum transfer associated with ionization, recombination, charge exchange, and related collisional processes; unlike [toroidal ion momentum source](name:toroidal_ion_momentum_source), it is not summed over ion charge states. Its corresponding poloidal projection is [poloidal ion charge state momentum source](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_source).

Sign convention: Positive when the sourced momentum points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: vertical_width_of_beamlet_group
items.description: Full vertical cross-sectional extent of a neutral-beam-injection beamlet group at the injection unit’s source surface.
items.documentation:
The quantity is the full vertical geometric width occupied collectively by the beamlets in a neutral-beam-injection group at the injection unit’s grounded-grid source surface.

The width is defined by the separation of the uppermost and lowermost beamlet-group boundaries:

$$
w_v = Z_{\mathrm{top}} - Z_{\mathrm{bottom}}
$$

where $w_v$ is the vertical beamlet-group width, $Z_{\mathrm{top}}$ and $Z_{\mathrm{bottom}}$ are the upper and lower vertical coordinates of the group boundary, and $Z$ is the vertical coordinate in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame; $R$ is major radius and $\phi$ is toroidal angle.

This quantity applies to the aggregate cross-sectional envelope of the beamlet group at the source surface, not to an individual beamlet. It represents the full width rather than a half-width, local spread, or width evaluated at another position along the beam line.

The width changes along the beam line as the beamlets converge. It is therefore distinct from the [vertical focal length of the beamlet group](name:vertical_focal_length_of_beamlet_group), which is the distance to the point of minimum vertical width rather than the width itself.

items.name: methane_source_rate
items.description: Instantaneous rate of neutral methane-molecule delivery into the plasma vessel by gas injection, counted per molecule rather than as an equivalent-electron or elemental source.
items.documentation:
Methane source rate is the instantaneous rate at which neutral methane molecules are delivered to the plasma vessel by gas injection. It counts methane molecules directly, rather than converting them to equivalent electrons or to elemental carbon or hydrogen.

The source rate is defined by

$$
\dot{N}_{\mathrm{CH_4}}(t) = \frac{dN_{\mathrm{CH_4}}(t)}{dt}
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{CH_4}}(t)$ is the cumulative number of methane molecules delivered by gas injection and $t$ is time. The quantity is distinct from the [methane carbon-13 source rate](name:methane_carbon_13_source_rate), which applies specifically to carbon-13-labeled methane.

items.name: ratio_of_volume_averaged_tungsten_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density
items.description: Dimensionless tungsten abundance ratio equal to the plasma-volume-averaged elemental tungsten density divided by the plasma-volume-averaged electron density.
items.documentation:
Dimensionless tungsten abundance ratio equal to the plasma-volume-averaged elemental tungsten density divided by the plasma-volume-averaged electron density. It compares the charge-state-summed tungsten-ion population with the free-electron population in the same plasma volume.

The ratio is defined from the two volume averages over the plasma volume $V$ as

$$
a_{\mathrm{W},V}
=
\frac{\langle n_{\mathrm{W}}\rangle_V}{\langle n_e\rangle_V}
=
\frac{V^{-1}\int_V \sum_{z=1}^{74} n_{\mathrm{W}^{z+}}(\mathbf{x})\, dV}{V^{-1}\int_V n_e(\mathbf{x})\, dV}
$$

where $a_{\mathrm{W},V}$ denotes this tungsten abundance ratio, $V$ denotes the plasma volume enclosed by the last closed flux surface over which both averages are formed, $\langle n_{\mathrm{W}}\rangle_V$ is the [volume-averaged tungsten density](name:volume_averaged_tungsten_density), $\langle n_e\rangle_V$ is the [volume-averaged electron density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density), $n_{\mathrm{W}^{z+}}(\mathbf{x})$ is the local number density of tungsten ions in charge state $z$ at position $\mathbf{x}$, $n_e(\mathbf{x})$ is the local free-electron number density, $z=1,\ldots,74$ indexes the positive tungsten ionization states, and $dV$ is the volume element.

The scope is the confined plasma volume: both numerator and denominator use the same volume and the same volume-averaging operation. The tungsten population is elemental tungsten in positive ionization states, summed over charge state; neutral tungsten is excluded. The aggregation is the ratio of the two volume averages, not the volume average of the local ratio $n_{\mathrm{W}}/n_e$, and the quantity is defined only when $\langle n_e\rangle_V$ is nonzero.

This ratio is an unweighted tungsten-nucleus abundance relative to free electrons; it is not a charge-weighted tungsten contribution to electron density and is not an effective-charge measure. It is the tungsten member of the same volume-averaged composition-ratio family as the [deuterium-tritium abundance ratio](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_deuterium_tritium_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density) and the [carbon abundance ratio](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_carbon_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density), which replace the tungsten numerator with the corresponding species volume average while retaining the same electron-density denominator.

items.name: vertical_electron_velocity
items.description: Signed height-axis component of the local electron-fluid bulk flow in the edge plasma, parallel to the toroidal symmetry axis.
items.documentation:
The vertical electron velocity is the height-axis projection of the local bulk electron flow in the edge plasma. It represents directed electron motion after averaging over particle velocities, rather than random thermal motion.

The defining projection is

$$
u_{e,Z} = \mathbf{u}_e \cdot \hat{\mathbf{z}}
$$

where $u_{e,Z}$ is the vertical electron velocity, $\mathbf{u}_e$ is the local bulk [electron velocity](name:electron_velocity), and $\hat{\mathbf{z}}$ is the unit vector along the vertical symmetry axis. The right-handed cylindrical frame is $(R,\phi,Z)$, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The underlying bulk flow is the particle-density-weighted mean electron velocity at each position; no spatial averaging is implied. This signed component is distinct from the electron speed, thermal velocity spread, and particle flux. The vertical direction is geometric and need not coincide with the local magnetic-field direction.

Together with [radial electron velocity](name:radial_electron_velocity) and [toroidal electron velocity](name:toroidal_electron_velocity), it specifies the cylindrical components of the electron-flow vector.

Sign convention: Positive when the electron bulk flow has a component toward increasing vertical height $Z$.

items.name: y_first_measurement_direction_unit_vector_of_strain_gauge
items.description: Y-axis component of the unit vector along the first measurement axis of a structural strain-rosette gage, resolved in the right-handed Cartesian (x, y, z) frame.
items.documentation:
Y-axis component of the unit vector along the first measurement axis of a structural strain-rosette gage is the scalar projection of that oriented measurement-axis unit vector onto the $\hat{y}$ basis direction of the right-handed Cartesian $(x, y, z)$ frame with basis $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$. It is a direction cosine describing gage orientation, not a strain value.

The component is defined by the dot product:

$$
u_{1y} = \mathbf{u}_1 \cdot \hat{y}
$$

where $u_{1y}$ is this y-axis component, $\mathbf{u}_1$ is the unit vector along the first measurement axis of the structural strain-rosette gage, and $\hat{y}$ is the y basis vector of the right-handed Cartesian $(x, y, z)$ frame.

Together with the corresponding x-axis component and z-axis component, it specifies the full orientation of the first measurement axis and satisfies the unit-vector normalization $u_{1x}^2 + u_{1y}^2 + u_{1z}^2 = 1$. It is distinct from the y-axis component of the unit vector along the second measurement axis.

Sign convention: Positive when the unit vector along the first measurement axis of the structural strain-rosette gage has a component in the $+\hat{y}$ direction of the right-handed Cartesian $(x, y, z)$ frame.

items.name: toroidal_ion_momentum_flux
items.description: Toroidal ion momentum flux is the area-averaged transport of toroidal linear momentum across a magnetic flux surface for one ion species, summed over ionic charge states.
items.documentation:
Toroidal ion momentum flux describes transport of the toroidally directed component of linear [momentum](name:momentum) across a magnetic flux surface. Toroidal specifies the transported momentum component, not the direction in which that momentum crosses the surface.

The surface-area-averaged flux is defined by:

$$
\Gamma_{i,\phi} = \frac{1}{A_\rho}\int_{S_\rho} \hat{\phi}\cdot\mathsf{T}_i\cdot\hat{n}_\rho\,dA
$$

where $\Gamma_{i,\phi}$ is this toroidal ion momentum flux, $i$ identifies the selected ion species, $S_\rho$ is the magnetic flux surface labeled by the outward-increasing flux label $\rho$, $A_\rho$ is its total area, $dA$ is a surface-area element, and $\hat{n}_\rho$ is its outward unit normal. The tensor $\mathsf{T}_i$ is the selected species' linear-momentum flux tensor, summed over ionic charge states, with its first index denoting the momentum component and its second the transport direction. The unit vector $\hat{\phi}$ points along increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius and $Z$ is vertical height.

The flux includes convective transport and pressure, viscous, or turbulent stress contributions; it is not restricted to diffusive transport. It applies to one ion species and excludes neutrals and other ion species. Summing the corresponding [charge-state-resolved fluxes](name:toroidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux) over all ionic charge states gives this species-level flux. Summing over ion species gives the toroidal component of the total [ion momentum flux](name:ion_momentum_flux).

This quantity is a flux per unit surface area, not a surface-integrated transport rate. It transports linear momentum rather than angular momentum and is distinct from the local angular-momentum source represented by [toroidal ion torque density](name:toroidal_ion_torque_density).

Sign convention: Positive when the net transport carries momentum directed along increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ outward, or oppositely directed momentum inward.

items.name: normalized_particle_perturbed_pressure
items.description: Normalized gyrotropic pressure-tensor moment of the perturbed particle distribution for a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode, decomposed into components parallel and perpendicular to the background magnetic field.
items.documentation:
The normalized particle perturbed pressure is a gyrotropic vector quantity representing the pressure fluctuation of the physical particle population in a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode, decomposed into components parallel and perpendicular to the equilibrium magnetic field $\mathbf{B}$, each expressed dimensionlessly as a ratio to a reference thermal pressure $p_\mathrm{ref}$.

For species $s$, the parallel and perpendicular components are the second velocity-space moments of the perturbed particle distribution function $\delta f_s$:

$$
\hat{p}_{\parallel,s} = \frac{m_s}{p_\mathrm{ref}} \int v_\parallel^2 \, \delta f_s \, d^3v, \qquad \hat{p}_{\perp,s} = \frac{m_s}{2 \, p_\mathrm{ref}} \int v_\perp^2 \, \delta f_s \, d^3v
$$

where $m_s$ is the species mass, $v_\parallel$ and $v_\perp$ are velocities parallel and perpendicular to $\mathbf{B}$, and $p_\mathrm{ref} = n_\mathrm{ref} T_\mathrm{ref}$ is evaluated at the outboard midplane.

Unlike the corresponding gyroaveraged gyrocenter perturbed pressure, this quantity is built from the full particle distribution function, implicitly incorporating finite-Larmor-radius corrections through the particle-to-gyrocenter coordinate transformation. The isotropic scalar parent particle_perturbed_pressure is recovered as the trace average $\hat{p}_s = (\hat{p}_{\parallel,s} + 2\hat{p}_{\perp,s})/3$. The parallel_normalized_particle_perturbed_pressure and [perpendicular_normalized_particle_perturbed_pressure](name:perpendicular_normalized_particle_perturbed_pressure) components together encode the pressure anisotropy of the eigenmode, with the ratio $\hat{p}_{\parallel,s}/\hat{p}_{\perp,s}$ quantifying deviation from local thermodynamic equilibrium relevant to mirror-mode and fire-hose stability.

items.name: back_surface_neutron_flux
items.description: Back-surface neutron flux is the scalar energy flux carried by fusion neutrons escaping through the back surface of an applicable component or module. It is aggregated over neutron energies, fusion reaction channels, and reacting populations; it is not a maximum over the surface.
items.documentation:
Back-surface neutron flux is the scalar surface density of power carried by fusion neutrons crossing outward through the back surface of the applicable component or module. It characterizes the local neutron energy load at that rear surface, not a vector flux and not a surface aggregate.

The local scalar flux $q_n$ at a point $\boldsymbol{r}$ on the back surface is defined by

$$
q_n(\boldsymbol{r}) = \frac{dP_{n,\mathrm{out}}}{dA}(\boldsymbol{r})
$$

where $q_n$ is the back-surface neutron flux, $\boldsymbol{r}$ is a point on the back surface, $P_{n,\mathrm{out}}$ is the power carried by fusion neutrons crossing outward through that surface, and $A$ is area on the back surface.

The scope is the back surface only: the surface opposite the front or plasma-facing side of the object under consideration. The quantity is aggregated over neutron energies, fusion reaction channels, and reacting populations unless a more specific standard name states a narrower selection.

This quantity excludes neutron source strength in a volume, total neutron power integrated over an area, flux at other surfaces, and any extremum selected over the back surface. A surface aggregate such as [maximum back-surface neutron flux](name:maximum_of_back_surface_neutron_flux) is obtained by taking the maximum value of this quantity over the applicable back surface; the maximum operation is not part of `back_surface_neutron_flux` itself.

The area integral of $q_n$ over a chosen part of the back surface gives the neutron power crossing outward through that part, while the local value remains the surface-density quantity defined at each point.

items.name: toroidal_vacuum_magnetic_vector_potential
items.description: Toroidal (φ) component of the gage-dependent vacuum magnetic vector potential produced solely by toroidal-field coil currents in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
The toroidal component $A_\u03c6$ of the vacuum magnetic vector potential is the projection of $\mathbf{A}_\mathrm{vac}$ onto the toroidal direction $\hat{\phi}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. It represents the toroidally directed external-source contribution produced solely by toroidal-field coil currents, excluding the contribution generated by plasma currents.

The component is defined by

$$
A_\phi = \mathbf{A}_\mathrm{vac} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $A_\phi$ is the toroidal component, $\mathbf{A}_\mathrm{vac}$ is the vacuum magnetic vector potential, and $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing toroidal angle. Here, $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

This scalar is the signed toroidal projection of the gage-dependent [vacuum magnetic vector potential](name:vacuum_magnetic_vector_potential), not its magnitude or full vector. Together with the [radial vacuum magnetic vector potential](name:radial_vacuum_magnetic_vector_potential) and [vertical vacuum magnetic vector potential](name:vertical_vacuum_magnetic_vector_potential), it provides the component decomposition of the vacuum vector potential; plasma-current contributions remain excluded.

Sign convention: Positive when $A_\phi$ points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: radius_of_bragg_crystal
items.description: Geometric distance from the center of a circular Bragg-crystal aperture to the edge of its active diffracting surface.
items.documentation:
The Bragg-crystal aperture radius is the transverse geometric extent of the circular active diffracting surface, measured from its center to its circumferential edge. It describes aperture size rather than the curvature of the crystal substrate.

For a boundary point of the aperture, the radius is defined by

$$
r_{\mathrm{ap}} = \left\lVert \mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{edge}} - \mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{center}} \right\rVert
$$

where $r_{\mathrm{ap}}$ is the aperture radius, and $\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{edge}}$ and $\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{center}}$ are position vectors in the aperture plane, with $r_{\mathrm{ap}}$ expressed in meters.

For an ideal circular aperture, this distance is the same for every boundary point. It is analogous to the [radius of a diagnostic aperture](name:radius_of_diagnostic_aperture), but must not be confused with the toroidal curvature of the Bragg crystal or its [vertical curvature](name:vertical_curvature_of_bragg_crystal).

items.name: toroidal_magnetization_of_ferritic_element
items.description: Toroidal component of the ferritic-element magnetization vector: the signed projection of the effective magnetization assigned to a discrete ferritic element onto the positive toroidal direction in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame. This is the element-level convention, not a pointwise bulk-material magnetization field.
items.documentation:
Toroidal component of the ferritic-element magnetization vector is the signed projection of the effective magnetization assigned to a discrete ferritic element onto the toroidal basis direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The projection is defined by:

$$
M_\phi^{\mathrm{fe}} = \mathbf{M}^{\mathrm{fe}} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $\mathbf{M}^{\mathrm{fe}}$ is the ferritic-element magnetization vector assigned to the element, $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing toroidal angle, and $M_\phi^{\mathrm{fe}}$ is this toroidal component.

In this family, ferritic-element magnetization denotes the effective magnetization attributed to the individual ferritic element for its magnetic source strength. It is not the pointwise bulk magnetization field inside the material, and it is distinct from material properties such as magnetic permeability. Together with the [radial component](name:radial_magnetization_of_ferritic_element) and [vertical component](name:vertical_magnetization_of_ferritic_element), it forms the three cylindrical components of the same effective ferritic-element magnetization vector.

Sign convention: Positive when $M_\phi^{\mathrm{fe}}$ points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ (counter-clockwise viewed from above $+\hat{Z}$).

items.name: current_of_rogowski_coil
items.description: Signed conventional current threading a Rogowski-coil winding contour, with orientation set by the coil's assigned normal.
items.documentation:
Signed conventional current threading a Rogowski-coil winding contour is the net conventional electric current crossing an oriented surface bounded by that contour. The surface orientation is specified by the coil's assigned normal and the associated right-hand rule for the contour.

The enclosed current is defined by the surface integral of conventional current density:

$$
I_{\mathrm{enc}} = \int_S \mathbf{J} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}}\, dS
$$

where $S$ is any surface whose boundary is the Rogowski-coil contour, $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ is the assigned unit normal to that surface, and $\mathbf{J}$ is the conventional electric current density.

This is an enclosed-current quantity, not the electrical current carried by the Rogowski-coil sensor winding. In the Rogowski-coil principle, the induced winding voltage is proportional to $dI_{\mathrm{enc}}/dt$; $I_{\mathrm{enc}}$ is the current whose time variation drives that signal.

Sign convention: Positive when the net conventional current crosses the oriented surface in the direction of the assigned normal.

items.name: y_minor_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone
items.description: Y component of the unit vector along the minor axis of an elliptic shatter cone, resolved in the right-handed Cartesian (x, y, z) frame.
items.documentation:
The minor-axis unit vector specifies one orientation of the elliptic shatter cone. This quantity is its signed projection onto the Cartesian y direction, complementing the [x minor-axis component](name:x_minor_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone) and [z minor-axis component](name:z_minor_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone).

The component is defined by

$$
u_y = \mathbf{u}_{\mathrm{minor}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{y}}
$$

where $\mathbf{u}_{\mathrm{minor}}$ is the unit vector along the shatter-cone minor axis and $\hat{\mathbf{y}}$ is the y-directed unit vector in the right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$ frame. The complete minor-axis vector has unit norm, so its components satisfy $u_x^2 + u_y^2 + u_z^2 = 1$.

items.name: neon_prefill_count
items.description: Neon prefill count is the total amount of neutral neon (Ne) introduced before plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count with 10 equivalent electrons per atom.
items.documentation:
Neon prefill count is the total amount of neutral neon (Ne) introduced during the prefill phase before plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count. Each neutral neon atom contributes 10 equivalent electrons.

The equivalent-electron count is defined by

$$
N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{Ne,prefill}} = Z_{\mathrm{Ne}}N_{\mathrm{Ne,prefill}} = 10N_{\mathrm{Ne,prefill}} = \int_{t_0}^{t_{\mathrm{bd}}}10\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Ne}}(t)\,dt
$$

where $N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{Ne,prefill}}$ is the neon equivalent-electron count and $N_{\mathrm{Ne,prefill}}$ is the accumulated neutral-neon atom count, both pure counts; $Z_{\mathrm{Ne}}=10$ is the atomic number of neon; $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Ne}}$ is the neutral-neon atom introduction rate in atoms s$^{-1}$; and $t_0$ and $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ are the prefill start and plasma-breakdown times, with $t$ in s.

This quantity includes only neutral neon introduced before breakdown and excludes wall recycling, neutral-beam or pellet fueling, later gas injection, and retained or ionized inventory. The equivalent-electron convention is an accounting normalization based on neutral atomic composition, not a statement that the gas is fully ionized during prefill.
