It is the neon component of [prefill_count](name:prefill_count); [accumulated_neon_count](name:accumulated_neon_count) represents distinct post-breakdown accumulation, while [argon_prefill_count](name:argon_prefill_count) applies the same convention to a different noble gas.

items.name: resistance_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna
items.description: Resistance of an ion-cyclotron heating antenna is the real part of the effective radio-frequency loading impedance at the antenna feed reference plane. It represents the resistive component associated with power coupled to the plasma and dissipative antenna losses.
items.documentation:
Resistance of an ion-cyclotron heating antenna is the real part of the effective radio-frequency loading impedance presented by the antenna at its feed reference plane. It characterizes the component of the antenna load that absorbs radio-frequency power, including plasma loading and intrinsic dissipative losses, distinct from the reactive energy storage represented by antenna capacitance or inductance.

The antenna loading impedance is decomposed into resistive and reactive parts as:

$$
Z_\mathrm{ant} = R_\mathrm{ant} + i X_\mathrm{ant}
$$

where $Z_\mathrm{ant}$ is the complex antenna loading impedance, $R_\mathrm{ant}$ is the antenna resistance in ohms, $X_\mathrm{ant}$ is the antenna reactance in ohms, and $i^2=-1$.

For a sinusoidal strap current, the resistive power associated with this load is $P_\mathrm{res}=R_\mathrm{ant} I_\mathrm{rms}^2$, where $P_\mathrm{res}$ is in watts and $I_\mathrm{rms}$ is the root-mean-square wave current of the antenna strap in amperes. This quantity is a feed-plane impedance component and is not itself a forward, reflected, or net power; those powers describe traveling-wave energy flow in the connected radio-frequency circuit.

items.name: ratio_of_volume_averaged_oxygen_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density
items.description: Volume-averaged oxygen ion density relative to volume-averaged electron density for the plasma, with oxygen summed over ionized charge states and neutral oxygen excluded.
items.documentation:
Volume-averaged oxygen ion density relative to volume-averaged electron density is a scalar oxygen impurity fraction for the plasma. It compares the charge-state-summed volume average of ionized oxygen number density with the corresponding volume average of electron number density over the same averaging volume.

The ratio is defined by

$$
f_O = \frac{\left\langle \sum_{q=1}^{8} n_{O^{q+}} \right\rangle_V}{\langle n_e \rangle_V}
$$

where $f_O$ is this oxygen-to-electron density ratio, $\langle\cdot\rangle_V$ denotes a volume average over the averaging volume $V$, $q$ is the oxygen charge-state index, $n_{O^{q+}}$ is the local number density of oxygen ions in charge state $q+$, and $n_e$ is the local electron number density. The denominator $\langle n_e\rangle_V$ is the [volume-averaged electron density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density).

The numerator is summed over ionized oxygen charge states $O^{1+}$ through $O^{8+}$ and excludes neutral oxygen. This quantity is a single scalar composition fraction formed from volume-averaged populations; it is distinct from a local [oxygen density](name:oxygen_density), from a [line-averaged oxygen density](name:line_averaged_oxygen_density), and from a neutral-inclusive [volume-averaged oxygen density](name:volume_averaged_oxygen_density) when that quantity includes neutral oxygen.

The essential relationship is normalization: the charge-state-summed volume-averaged oxygen ion density is divided by the [volume-averaged electron density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density), so the result represents oxygen ion abundance relative to the electron population rather than an absolute density.

items.name: displacement_of_passive_structure
items.description: Displacement of a passive structure is the signed linear displacement of a selected point or defined surface target on a passive component relative to a reference configuration, projected along a defined positive direction.
items.documentation:
Displacement of a passive structure is the signed scalar component of the motion of a selected material point, attachment point, or defined reference point on a passive structural component relative to a reference configuration. It is the passive-structure instance of mechanical displacement, not an absolute position, velocity, acceleration, or strain.

The signed projected displacement is defined by

$$
u(t) = \left[\mathbf{r}(t) - \mathbf{r}_\mathrm{ref}\right] \cdot \hat{\mathbf{e}}_u
$$

where $u(t)$ is the scalar displacement, $\mathbf{r}(t)$ is the current position vector of the selected point, $\mathbf{r}_\mathrm{ref}$ is the position vector of the same point in the reference configuration, and $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_u$ is the unit vector defining the positive direction of the displacement component. All vectors and the unit direction are expressed in the same right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$ frame, with $\hat{z}$ vertical.

The selected point, reference configuration, and positive direction are part of the semantic definition of any instance. An undeformed, surveyed, calibrated, initial, or previous-time configuration may serve as $\mathbf{r}_\mathrm{ref}$ only if that choice is fixed; changing it changes the displacement, and using a previous-time reference defines an incremental displacement over the interval. A single value describes one projected local displacement; deformation or strain requires spatial variation of displacement or a separate deformation measure.

Sign convention: Positive when the selected point is displaced from $\mathbf{r}_\mathrm{ref}$ in the direction of $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_u$.

items.name: inner_squareness_of_flux_surface
items.description: Dimensionless Luce shape coefficient quantifying how much the high-field-side (inner) corners of a nested magnetic flux surface deviate from a reference ellipse; positive values indicate a boxier corner, negative values a more diamond-like or indented corner.
items.documentation:
The inner squareness of a flux surface is the dimensionless Luce (2013) shape coefficient that characterizes how much the high-field-side (inboard, smaller major radius) corners of a nested toroidal magnetic flux surface depart from a reference ellipse sharing the same center, horizontal half-width, and [elongation](name:elongation_of_flux_surface). It is the inboard counterpart within the [squareness_of_flux_surface](name:squareness_of_flux_surface) family, complementing the outboard variants [upper_outer_squareness_of_flux_surface](name:upper_outer_squareness_of_flux_surface) and [lower_outer_squareness_of_flux_surface](name:lower_outer_squareness_of_flux_surface). This parent quantity abstracts over the quadrant-resolved coefficients [upper_inner_squareness_of_flux_surface](name:upper_inner_squareness_of_flux_surface) and [lower_inner_squareness_of_flux_surface](name:lower_inner_squareness_of_flux_surface), which independently describe the upper and lower high-field-side corners.

The coefficient $\zeta$ enters the parametric flux-surface shape model as an additional harmonic beyond elongation $\kappa$ and triangularity $\delta$, evaluated at the high-field-side corners of the poloidal cross-section in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius and $Z$ is vertical height. A value of zero recovers the reference ellipse precisely; deviations capture corner shaping not expressible through $\kappa$ and $\delta$ alone.

The inner squareness is inferred from equilibrium reconstruction by fitting closed flux-surface contours to a multi-parameter shape model. Asymmetry between upper and lower inner quadrants can arise in vertically asymmetric or diverted configurations, motivating the quadrant-resolved child quantities.

items.name: ammonia_prefill_count
items.description: Ammonia prefill count is the total amount of NH3 introduced before plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count of 10 per neutral molecule.
items.documentation:
Ammonia prefill count is the total amount of neutral ammonia, NH3, introduced before plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count. Each neutral NH3 molecule contributes ten count units: seven from nitrogen and one from each of its three hydrogen atoms.

The count is defined by the accumulated molecular amount over the prefill interval:

$$
N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{NH_3,prefill}} = 10N_{\mathrm{NH_3,prefill}} = \int_{t_0}^{t_\mathrm{bd}} 10\dot{N}_{\mathrm{NH_3}}(t)\,dt
$$

where $N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{NH_3,prefill}}$ is the equivalent-electron count, $N_{\mathrm{NH_3,prefill}}$ is the accumulated number of ammonia molecules, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{NH_3}}$ is the ammonia injection rate in molecules per second, and $t_0$ and $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ are the start of prefill and plasma-breakdown times in seconds.

This species-specific contribution is included in the common prebreakdown bookkeeping of [prefill_count](name:prefill_count). Ammonia introduced after breakdown is excluded and is represented by [accumulated_ammonia_count](name:accumulated_ammonia_count).

items.name: plasma_pressure_real_part
items.description: Plasma pressure real part is the real quadrature of a complex scalar representation of isotropic plasma pressure. For perturbation eigenfunctions, it is the signed real component of the pressure perturbation, not the full complex eigenfunction.
items.documentation:
Plasma pressure real part is the scalar real quadrature of a complex representation of isotropic plasma pressure. It represents the component obtained after the phase convention for the complex pressure quantity has been fixed, and it is distinct from the complete complex quantity.

The real part is defined by applying the real-part operator to the corresponding complex plasma-pressure quantity:

$$
p_R = \operatorname{Re}(\tilde{p})
$$

where $p_R$ is the plasma pressure real part, $\tilde{p}$ is the corresponding complex scalar plasma-pressure quantity, and $\operatorname{Re}$ denotes extraction of the real component.

This parent quantity is restricted to real-part quantities of isotropic plasma pressure and does not by itself specify perturbation order, Fourier-mode labeling, phase normalization, or spatial locus. It applies to the plasma scalar pressure field; it is not a species-resolved pressure, a pressure-tensor component, or an anisotropic-pressure component.

It excludes the imaginary quadrature, modulus, phase, and complete complex pressure quantity. More specific children add the physics qualifier while preserving the same real-part operation; for example, [perturbed plasma pressure real part](name:perturbed_plasma_pressure_real_part) is the real component of a complex first-order plasma-pressure perturbation eigenfunction. If the corresponding complex quantity is written as $\tilde{p}=p_R+i p_I$, then $p_I$ is its imaginary quadrature and $i$ is the imaginary unit, while this name denotes only $p_R$.

Sign convention: Positive when the selected real quadrature denotes an increase of isotropic plasma pressure relative to the reference pressure state.

items.name: poloidal_neutral_state_particle_convection_velocity
items.description: Signed effective poloidal velocity coefficient for density-proportional convective particle transport of a specified neutral state in edge plasma.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the effective coefficient of density-proportional convective particle transport for a specified neutral state, projected onto the poloidal direction. It represents directed drift or pinch transport after density-gradient-driven diffusive transport has been separated.

The poloidal convective particle flux is defined by

$$
\Gamma_{n,s}^{\mathrm{conv,pol}} = n_s v_{n,s}^{\mathrm{conv,pol}}
$$

where $\Gamma_{n,s}^{\mathrm{conv,pol}}$ is the poloidal convective particle flux, $n_s$ is the particle density of the specified neutral state, and $v_{n,s}^{\mathrm{conv,pol}}$ is this effective velocity coefficient. The quantity is the poloidal component of [neutral state particle convection velocity](name:neutral_state_particle_convection_velocity), not the complete particle flux and not the diffusive transport coefficient. Its species-state and particle-channel meaning distinguishes it from the analogous [poloidal ion charge-state convection velocity](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_convection_velocity).

items.name: neon_density
items.description: Number density of neon impurity ions, summed over the included ionization states; line-averaged and volume-averaged forms express the same elemental content.
items.documentation:
Neon density is the number of neon impurity ions per unit volume, summed over all included charged ionization states. It represents elemental neon content rather than the density of one selected charge state; neutral neon atoms are excluded.

$$
n_{\mathrm{Ne}} = \sum_{z \in \mathcal{Z}_{\mathrm{Ne}}} n_{\mathrm{Ne}^{z+}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Ne}}$ is the charge-state-summed neon ion density, $n_{\mathrm{Ne}^{z+}}$ is the density of neon ions in charge state $z+$, and $\mathcal{Z}_{\mathrm{Ne}}$ is the set of included charged ionization states.

This species-specific quantity is a member of density. The same charge-state-summed field may be spatially averaged; [volume_averaged_neon_density](name:volume_averaged_neon_density) represents its volume average, while a charge-state-resolved quantity such as [ion_charge_state_density](name:ion_charge_state_density) selects one ionization state and is not equivalent.

items.name: toroidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_convection_velocity
items.description: Toroidal component of the momentum-convection velocity for ions of one specified species and charge state, evaluated at the maximum-major-radius point of each magnetic flux surface.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the toroidal component of the velocity associated with momentum convection for ions of one selected species and charge state. It is a velocity component, not an angular rotation frequency.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height, the component is the projection

$$
v_{s,q,\phi} = \mathbf{v}_{s,q} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $v_{s,q,\phi}$ is this quantity, $\mathbf{v}_{s,q}$ is the momentum-convection velocity vector for ion species $s$ and charge state $q$, $s$ identifies the ion species, $q$ identifies its charge state, and $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing toroidal angle.

The quantity is resolved for one ion species and one charge state and is evaluated at the point of maximum major radius on each magnetic flux surface, not as a surface average. It is not summed over charge states; the species-level [toroidal ion momentum convection velocity](name:toroidal_ion_momentum_convection_velocity) is the density-weighted mean over all charge states. This scalar is the toroidal component of the [ion charge-state momentum convection velocity](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_convection_velocity) vector and is distinct from its [radial component](name:radial_ion_charge_state_momentum_convection_velocity), which is along $\hat{R}$. It is a linear velocity component, distinct from the [toroidal ion charge-state rotation frequency](name:toroidal_ion_charge_state_rotation_frequency), an angular rate.

Sign convention: Positive when the velocity component points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: total_momentum_source
items.description: Directed rate of momentum transfer to or from all included particle populations, represented as an area-normalized vector source density.
items.documentation:
A momentum source density represents the directed transfer of momentum caused by physical processes acting on a plasma population or one of its resolved states. The total quantity retains the vector direction of the net momentum-transfer rate while aggregating the included particle populations.

The aggregate source is defined by

$$
\mathbf{S}_{p} = \sum_s \frac{\mathrm{d}\mathbf{P}_{\mathrm{src},s}}{\mathrm{d}A\,\mathrm{d}t}
$$

where $\mathbf{S}_{p}$ is the total momentum source density, $\mathbf{P}_{\mathrm{src},s}$ is the momentum transferred by source processes to or from population $s$, and $A$ is the surface over which the source is normalized. The sum includes only the particle populations specified by the physical scope of the quantity. Directional projections, such as [radial total momentum source](name:radial_total_momentum_source), are components of this vector quantity, while [momentum source](name:momentum_source) provides the broader family context.

items.name: torque_due_to_neutral_beam_shinethrough
items.description: Vector torque associated with angular momentum carried away by neutral beam particles that traverse the plasma without ionization. It represents the shinethrough contribution to the neutral-beam momentum balance, with components giving the direction and sense of the loss.
items.documentation:
Torque due to neutral beam shinethrough is the vector rate at which angular momentum is carried out of the plasma by injected neutral particles that traverse the plasma without ionization or absorption. It is a loss term for plasma angular momentum because the angular momentum of those unabsorbed particles is not deposited in the plasma.

The shinethrough torque is defined as the time rate of angular momentum carried by the shinethrough neutral-particle population:

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{st}} = \frac{d\boldsymbol{L}_{\mathrm{st}}}{dt}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{st}}$ is the torque due to neutral beam shinethrough and $\boldsymbol{L}_{\mathrm{st}}$ is the angular momentum carried by neutral beam particles after they pass through the plasma without ionization.

This vector quantity is the parent of component quantities such as the [toroidal torque due to neutral beam shinethrough](name:toroidal_torque_due_to_neutral_beam_shinethrough), which is its toroidal component in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. It excludes angular momentum deposited by absorbed neutral beam particles and torques due to other momentum-transfer mechanisms.

Sign convention: Positive when a component of $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{st}}$ is directed along the positive basis direction of that component; the toroidal component is positive in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: normalized_plasma_internal_inductance
items.description: Normalized internal inductance measures internal poloidal magnetic energy relative to squared plasma current and the plasma's geometric-axis major radius.
items.documentation:
Normalized internal inductance measures the poloidal magnetic energy contained within the entire plasma using the geometric-axis normalization known as li(3). It characterizes poloidal-field peaking associated with the plasma current distribution.

The normalized internal inductance $l_i$ is defined by

$$
l_i = \frac{2\int_V B_{\mathrm{p}}^2\,dV}{\mu_0^2 I_{\mathrm{p}}^2 R_{\mathrm{geo}}}
$$

where $B_{\mathrm{p}}$ is the poloidal magnetic-field magnitude, $V$ is the plasma volume, $dV$ is a volume element, $\mu_0$ is the vacuum permeability, $I_{\mathrm{p}}$ is the total toroidal plasma current, and $R_{\mathrm{geo}}$ is the major radius of the plasma's geometric axis.

The integral covers the full plasma volume and excludes magnetic energy outside the plasma and energy associated with the toroidal magnetic field. The normalization requires nonzero plasma current and uses the geometric axis rather than the magnetic axis.

The corresponding dimensional internal inductance $L_i$ satisfies $L_i = \mu_0 R_{\mathrm{geo}}l_i/2$. This normalization distinguishes the quantity from dimensional [plasma inductance](name:plasma_inductance).

items.name: toroidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field
items.description: Toroidal perturbed plasma magnetic field is the toroidal component of the complex linear-MHD magnetic-field perturbation carried by the confined-plasma response about equilibrium.
items.documentation:
Toroidal perturbed plasma magnetic field is the toroidal component of the complex linear-MHD eigenfunction, or corresponding real perturbation, of the magnetic-field deviation carried by the confined-plasma response about an equilibrium field. It is the toroidal projection of the [perturbed plasma magnetic field](name:perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field) and excludes separately represented externally imposed vacuum perturbations.

The toroidal component is defined by

$$
\delta B_{\mathrm{pl},\phi}(\mathbf{x},t) = \delta\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{pl}}(\mathbf{x},t) \cdot \hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}
$$

where $\delta B_{\mathrm{pl},\phi}$ is the toroidal component, $\delta\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{pl}}$ is the plasma-response perturbation, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $t$ is time, and $\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}$ is the toroidal unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame with oriented basis $(\hat{\mathbf{R}},\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}},\hat{\mathbf{Z}})$. Here $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The response field is $\delta\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{pl}}=\mathbf{B}-\mathbf{B}_0-\delta\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{vac}}$, where $\mathbf{B}$ is total field, $\mathbf{B}_0$ is equilibrium field, and $\delta\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{vac}}$ is a separately represented vacuum perturbation. For a specified toroidal Fourier harmonic, the [real part](name:toroidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_real_part) and [imaginary part](name:toroidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_imaginary_part) are phase components of this same toroidal quantity.

Sign convention: Positive when the corresponding real-valued perturbation points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: outer_squareness_of_flux_surface
items.description: Dimensionless Luce shape coefficient for the outboard corners of nested magnetic flux surfaces, measuring signed departure from a co-centered reference ellipse across upper and lower quadrants.
items.documentation:
The outer squareness of a flux surface is the dimensionless Luce (2013) shape coefficient that characterizes how much the outboard (larger major radius) corners of a nested toroidal magnetic flux surface depart from a reference ellipse sharing the same center, horizontal half-width, and [elongation](name:elongation_of_flux_surface). It is the outboard counterpart within the [squareness_of_flux_surface](name:squareness_of_flux_surface) family, complementing the [inner squareness](name:inner_squareness_of_flux_surface), and abstracts over the quadrant-resolved coefficients [upper outer squareness](name:upper_outer_squareness_of_flux_surface) and [lower outer squareness](name:lower_outer_squareness_of_flux_surface).

At the modeled outboard corners, the reference condition is

$$
\zeta_{\rm out}=0 \Longleftrightarrow \mathcal{C}_{\rm out}=\mathcal{E}_{\rm out}
$$

where $\zeta_{\rm out}$ is the outer squareness coefficient, $\mathcal{C}_{\rm out}$ is the modeled outboard corner of the flux-surface cross-section, and $\mathcal{E}_{\rm out}$ is the corresponding reference ellipse. The cross-section is described in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

This quantity does not select either the upper or lower outboard quadrant; those quadrant-specific coefficients may differ for an up-down asymmetric flux surface. Positive values describe boxier outward corners, while negative values describe corners indented relative to the reference ellipse.

items.name: neutral_species_energy_flux
items.description: Neutral species energy flux is the signed neutral-species energy-flux-density vector; its projection normal to an oriented surface gives the crossing power per unit area for one specified neutral species, summed over all internal states.
items.documentation:
Neutral species energy flux is the signed energy-flux-density vector carried by one specified neutral atom or molecule species. Its projection onto an oriented surface normal gives the rate at which energy carried by that neutral species crosses the surface per unit area, summed over all internal states of the species and including convective and conductive contributions when those channels are in scope.

For an oriented surface with unit normal $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$, the signed surface-normal flux associated with the neutral-species energy flux $\mathbf{q}_{E,N_s}$ is defined by

$$
F_{E,N_s}^{(\hat{\mathbf{n}})} = \mathbf{q}_{E,N_s} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}}
$$

where $N_s$ labels the selected neutral species, the subscript $E$ denotes energy transport, $\mathbf{q}_{E,N_s}$ is the neutral-species energy-flux-density vector, $F_{E,N_s}^{(\hat{\mathbf{n}})}$ is its signed surface-normal projection, and $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ defines the positive crossing direction.

This quantity applies to one selected neutral species in the neutral population and is aggregated by summing contributions from all internal states of that species. It is species-resolved: it is not the all-neutral [neutral energy flux](name:neutral_energy_flux), not total plasma energy flux, not an electromagnetic Poynting flux, and not [electron energy flux](name:electron_energy_flux) or [ion energy flux](name:ion_energy_flux).

The vector may be projected onto specified directions to form directional components. [Poloidal neutral species energy flux](name:poloidal_neutral_species_energy_flux) is the poloidal directional component of this neutral-species vector, whereas this parent quantity does not itself select a poloidal, parallel, or surface-normal projection. When the same energy channels and internal-state aggregation are used, summing this species-resolved vector over neutral species gives the all-neutral [neutral energy flux](name:neutral_energy_flux).

Sign convention: Positive when the neutral-species energy-flux-density vector has a component in the chosen positive projection direction or chosen unit normal to an oriented surface.

items.name: volume_integrated_particle_source_rate
items.description: Volume-integrated particle source rate is the net number of particles added to a specified distribution per unit time by a source contribution over the plasma volume.
items.documentation:
Volume-integrated particle source rate is the net particle-number input to a specified particle distribution from a given source contribution, integrated over the plasma volume.

The defining volume integral is

$$
S(t) = \int_V s_p(\mathbf{x},t)\,d^3x
$$

where $S$ is the volume-integrated particle source rate, $t$ is time, $V$ is the plasma volume, $\mathbf{x}$ is physical position, $d^3x$ is the volume element, and $s_p$ is the local net particle source rate per physical volume. For a kinetic source term, $s_p$ is its velocity-space integral, the particle-number moment.

The rate applies to the species and population represented by the specified distribution. Volume integration does not imply summation over other distributions, species, or source mechanisms. For a distribution-function-driven contribution, it is the volume integral of the [particle source rate due to distribution-function-driven processes](name:particle_source_rate_due_to_distribution_function_driven), not its volume average.

No restriction to thermal particles or thermalization is implied. When the contribution describes thermalization, it counts transfer from fast particles into the thermal background, rather than particle creation in the combined populations; reverse transfer constitutes a sink for the thermal population.

Sign convention: Positive when the source contribution adds particles to the specified distribution; negative when it removes particles.

items.name: perturbed_plasma_temperature_real_part
items.description: In-phase component of the complex first-order plasma-temperature eigenfunction for a specified toroidal Fourier harmonic in linear MHD stability analysis.
items.documentation:
The quantity is the real, in-phase component of the first-order plasma-temperature perturbation associated with one toroidal Fourier harmonic. It is a component of the complex eigenfunction represented by perturbed plasma temperature.

The in-phase component is defined from the complex perturbation amplitude by

$$
\delta T_{\mathrm{R}} = \operatorname{Re}\!\left(\delta T\right)
$$

where $\delta T_{\mathrm{R}}$ is the real temperature-perturbation component and $\delta T$ is the full complex first-order temperature eigenfunction. The result depends on the phase reference chosen for the harmonic and excludes the quadrature component represented by the imaginary part. It is not the equilibrium temperature or the complete complex perturbation.

items.name: binormal_coordinate_of_correction_coil
items.description: Signed displacement of a correction-coil conductor outline vertex along the local Frenet–Serret binormal, measured from the conductor centerline.
items.documentation:
The binormal coordinate specifies the signed position of a correction-coil conductor cross-section outline vertex along the local Frenet–Serret binormal direction. Together with the [normal coordinate of the correction coil](name:normal_coordinate_of_correction_coil), it defines the vertex position in the cross-sectional plane.

For vertex position $\mathbf{r}_v$ and corresponding centerline position $\mathbf{r}_c$, the coordinate is

$$
b_v = (\mathbf{r}_v - \mathbf{r}_c) \cdot \hat{\mathbf{b}}
$$

where $b_v$ is the binormal coordinate in m, $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$ is the local unit binormal, and $\mathbf{r}_v$ and $\mathbf{r}_c$ are positions in m. The local Frenet–Serret triad is oriented so that $\hat{\mathbf{b}} = \hat{\mathbf{t}} \times \hat{\mathbf{n}}$, with $\hat{\mathbf{t}}$ the tangent and $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ the normal unit vector. This coordinate is a signed vertex displacement, not the full conductor cross-section height represented by the [height of the correction coil](name:height_of_correction_coil).

Sign convention: Positive when the vertex displacement from the conductor centerline points in the direction of the local unit binormal $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$.

items.name: hydrogen_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection
items.description: Instantaneous equivalent-electron hydrogen source rate delivered to the plasma vessel by gas injection systems; each hydrogen atom contributes one equivalent-electron count.
items.documentation:
The hydrogen source rate due to gas injection characterizes the instantaneous rate at which neutral hydrogen atoms are admitted to the plasma vessel by gas injection, expressed as an equivalent-electron count rate. Because hydrogen has atomic number one, each atom contributes one equivalent-electron count.

The defining relation is:

$$
\dot{S}_{\mathrm{H}} = Z_{\mathrm{H}}\dot{N}_{\mathrm{H}} = \dot{N}_{\mathrm{H}}, \qquad Z_{\mathrm{H}} = 1
$$

where $\dot{S}_{\mathrm{H}}$ is the equivalent-electron source rate, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{H}}$ is the neutral hydrogen-atom delivery rate in atoms per second, and $Z_{\mathrm{H}}$ is the hydrogen atomic number. This is the hydrogen component of the total [source rate due to gas injection](name:source_rate_due_to_gas_injection). Its time integral gives the accumulated hydrogen inventory [accumulated hydrogen count due to gas injection](name:accumulated_hydrogen_count_due_to_gas_injection).

Sign convention: Positive when hydrogen gas is being delivered into the vessel, increasing the equivalent-electron inventory.

items.name: vertical_coordinate_of_passive_loop_element
items.description: Vertical coordinate of a passive-loop element's geometry-defining point: the geometric center in oblique geometry or a specified endpoint in thick-line geometry, expressed as signed height in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
Vertical coordinate of a point associated with a passive-loop element is its signed position along the symmetry axis. It gives the geometric-center height for oblique geometry and the height of the specified endpoint for thick-line geometry.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is the vertical coordinate. The [vertical direction] is parallel to the toroidal symmetry axis, and the coordinate is defined by its projection:

$$
Z = \mathbf{x}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{z}}
$$

where $\mathbf{x}$ is the point's position vector relative to the coordinate origin and $\hat{\mathbf{z}}$ is the unit vector along the symmetry axis toward increasing $Z$.

The coordinate applies to the geometry-defining point for an individual passive-loop element; it is not an aggregate across elements. For thick-line geometry it refers to the specified endpoint, not the cross-sectional geometric center or an average over the cross-section. It specifies a location, not a transverse size such as the [thickness of the passive-loop element](name:thickness_of_passive_loop_element).

Sign convention: Positive when the point lies in the $+Z$ direction from the plane $Z=0$.

items.name: ion_average_temperature_at_limiter
items.description: Density-weighted mean kinetic temperature of all ion species and charge states on the plasma-facing side of a limiter, providing the ion component of the local average plasma temperature.
items.documentation:
The ion component of the local plasma temperature at a limiter is the density-weighted mean kinetic temperature of all positive ion species and charge states on the plasma-facing side of the limiter. It is the ion-specific component of average temperature at the limiter.

$$
T_{i,\mathrm{avg}} = \frac{\sum_s \sum_q n_{s,q} T_{s,q}}{\sum_s \sum_q n_{s,q}}
$$

where $s$ indexes ion species, $q$ indexes their positive charge states, $n_{s,q}$ is the corresponding ion number density, and $T_{s,q}$ is its kinetic temperature. The denominator is the [total ion density at the limiter](name:total_ion_density_at_limiter).

This quantity includes all ion species and charge states in the local plasma population and excludes electrons, neutral particles, and the solid limiter material. It is distinct from temperature at the limiter, which may denote a specified population or a different population aggregation.

items.name: parallel_ion_charge_state_convection_velocity
items.description: Parallel component of the effective convective velocity used for particle transport of a specified ion charge state in an edge plasma.
items.documentation:
Parallel component of the effective convective velocity used for particle transport of a specified ion charge state in an edge plasma. It is the field-aligned component of the vector defined by [ion charge-state convection velocity](name:ion_charge_state_convection_velocity) for that charge-state population.

The parallel component is defined by projection onto the local magnetic-field direction:

$$
v_{s,\parallel} = \mathbf{v}_s \cdot \hat{\mathbf{b}}
$$

where $v_{s,\parallel}$ is this parallel ion charge-state convection velocity, $\mathbf{v}_s$ is the [ion charge-state convection velocity](name:ion_charge_state_convection_velocity) vector for ion charge state $s$, and $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$ is the unit vector along the local magnetic-field vector $\mathbf{B}$.

The scope is charge-state resolved: $s$ denotes one specified ion charge state in the edge plasma, with no summation over charge states and no density-weighted mean over all charge states. The quantity is an effective particle-transport coefficient for that charge state, including the applicable thermal and nonthermal populations represented by the charge-state particle population.

It is distinct from the parallel ion fluid velocity or kinetic bulk velocity: it is the coefficient multiplying charge-state number density in convective particle transport and need not equal a moment of the particle velocity distribution. The total particle flux may also contain diffusive transport, which is excluded from this convective velocity.

The field-aligned convective particle-flux component $\Gamma_{s,\parallel,\mathrm{conv}}$ satisfies $\Gamma_{s,\parallel,\mathrm{conv}} = n_s v_{s,\parallel}$, where $\Gamma_{s,\parallel,\mathrm{conv}}$ is the field-aligned convective particle-flux component and $n_s$ is the number density of ion charge state $s$. Together with directional components such as the [poloidal ion charge-state convection velocity](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_convection_velocity) and [radial ion charge-state convection velocity](name:radial_ion_charge_state_convection_velocity), it is a projection of the same parent vector; the parallel direction is field-aligned and is not the poloidal tangent direction.

Sign convention: Positive when the effective convection velocity is directed along the local magnetic-field vector $\mathbf{B}$.

items.name: lower_bound_energy_of_detector_pixel
items.description: The lower bound energy of a detector pixel is the minimum photon energy accepted by that pixel's spectral bandpass in an X-ray crystal spectrometer.
items.documentation:
The lower bound energy of a detector pixel is the minimum photon energy at the low-energy edge of the spectral interval accepted by an individual detector pixel in an X-ray crystal spectrometer. It defines the lower endpoint of that pixel's photon-energy acceptance range.

This quantity applies to photons assigned to one detector pixel and represents a per-pixel spectral-channel boundary, not an integrated or averaged energy over multiple pixels or channels. It is distinct from the [energy of a detector pixel](name:energy_of_detector_pixel), which is the central or representative photon energy assigned to the pixel, and from the [upper bound energy of a detector pixel](name:upper_bound_energy_of_detector_pixel), which defines the high-energy edge. Together, the lower and upper bounds delimit the pixel's accepted photon-energy interval.

items.name: pfirsch_schlueter_current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
items.description: Pfirsch-Schlueter current density produced by diamagnetic drift in a magnetized plasma, representing the signed field-aligned return current that cancels the divergence of the pressure-gradient-driven diamagnetic current.
items.documentation:
Pfirsch-Schlueter current density due to diamagnetic drift is the signed field-aligned scalar return current associated with the pressure-gradient-driven current described by [current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift](name:current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift). It enforces charge-current continuity by canceling the divergence of the perpendicular diamagnetic current on a magnetic flux surface in toroidal geometry.

The scalar amplitude $j_{\mathrm{PS,dia}}$ is defined by the current-continuity condition

$$
\nabla \cdot \left(j_{\mathrm{PS,dia}}\mathbf{b}\right) = -\nabla \cdot \left(\frac{\mathbf{B} \times \nabla p}{B^2}\right)
$$

where $j_{\mathrm{PS,dia}}$ is the signed scalar Pfirsch-Schlueter current density due to diamagnetic drift, $\mathbf{b}=\mathbf{B}/B$ is the unit vector along the magnetic field, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic field, $B^2=\mathbf{B}\cdot\mathbf{B}$, and $p$ is the isotropic scalar plasma pressure.

This scalar denotes the amplitude multiplying the magnetic-field unit vector, not an independent vector current and not a cylindrical component. A flux-surface-constant parallel current component not required by the diamagnetic-current divergence is excluded; the component-oriented [parallel_pfirsch_schlueter_current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift](name:parallel_pfirsch_schlueter_current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift) denotes the parallel projection of the same field-aligned contribution.

Sign convention: Positive when conventional positive charge flows along the local magnetic field direction $\mathbf{B}$.

items.name: ion_charge_state_diffusivity
items.description: Ion charge-state diffusivity is the effective Fickian particle diffusivity for ions in a specified ionization state, without specifying a spatial projection.
items.documentation:
Ion charge-state diffusivity is the effective Fickian particle diffusivity for ions in a specified ionization state, without specifying a spatial projection. It is the scalar transport coefficient that relates the diffusive particle flux component of that charge state to the negative directional gradient of its number density.

For a chosen projection direction $\hat{\mathbf{e}}$, the defining Fickian relation is:

$$
\Gamma^{\mathrm{diff}}_{s,e} = -D_s\,\nabla_e n_s
$$

where $\Gamma^{\mathrm{diff}}_{s,e}$ is the projected diffusive particle flux density of charge state $s$, $D_s$ is this diffusivity, $n_s$ is the number density of charge state $s$, and $\nabla_e n_s = \hat{\mathbf{e}}\cdot\nabla n_s$ is the directional derivative of that number density. A positive flux component is directed along $+\hat{\mathbf{e}}$; the minus sign makes a positive diffusivity drive diffusive flux opposite to the projected density gradient.

This quantity is charge-state-resolved: it applies to a single ionization state rather than to the density-weighted mean over all charge states represented by ion diffusivity. It is the same physical coefficient as [ion charge-state diffusion coefficient](name:ion_charge_state_diffusion_coefficient) when that name is used for the same Fickian closure. Directionally specified counterparts include [radial ion charge-state diffusivity](name:radial_ion_charge_state_diffusivity) and [parallel ion charge-state diffusivity](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_diffusivity); convective or pinch transport, particle sources and sinks, and energy or momentum transport coefficients are separate quantities.

items.name: power_due_to_convection
items.description: Power deposited on plasma-facing surfaces by convective plasma particle flux, comprising thermal enthalpy and directed kinetic energy carried by streaming ions and electrons from the scrape-off layer.
items.documentation:
Convective power quantifies the energy transported to a plasma-facing surface by the bulk flow of plasma particles — ions, electrons, and neutral species — streaming along open magnetic field lines from the scrape-off layer to bounding material surfaces. It represents the convective channel of the total surface power balance, distinct from the conductive contribution driven by parallel temperature gradients and from radiative deposition.

The local convective heat-flux density summed over particle species $s$ is

$$
q_{\mathrm{conv}} = \sum_s n_s v_{\parallel,s} \left( \frac{\gamma_s}{\gamma_s - 1} k_B T_s + \frac{1}{2} m_s v_{\parallel,s}^2 \right)
$$

where $n_s$ is the number density, $v_{\parallel,s}$ the parallel flow speed, $\gamma_s$ the adiabatic index (5/3 for monatomic species), $T_s$ the temperature, and $m_s$ the particle mass. Integrating $q_{\mathrm{conv}}$ over the wetted surface area yields the total convective power in watts.

In experiments the convective power is inferred from Langmuir-probe measurements of particle flux and sheath-entrance temperature, or decomposed from total calorimetric measurements by subtracting the conductive fraction estimated via two-point model analysis. More specific realizations include [power at a single divertor target due to convection](name:power_at_divertor_target_due_to_convection), [convective power summed over all divertor targets](name:power_of_divertor_due_to_convection), and [convective power at the first wall](name:power_at_wall_due_to_convection). The full surface load integrating all channels is characterized by heat_flux_of_plasma_facing_component.

items.name: ion_momentum_source_rate
items.description: Ion momentum source rate is a scalar rate coefficient for proportional source, sink, or transfer terms in an ion momentum balance. Its population scope is ions, while child names may add qualifiers such as an implicit treatment; the parent does not choose a component, projection, isotope, or charge state.
items.documentation:
Ion momentum source rate is a scalar coefficient that parameterizes a source, sink, or transfer term proportional to an ion momentum quantity in an ion momentum-balance equation. Its population scope is ions, not electrons, neutrals, or a species-free momentum balance.

For a proportional contribution to an ion momentum source term, the defining relation is

$$
S_{M_i}^{(\gamma)} = \gamma_i M_i
$$

where $\gamma_i$ is the ion momentum source rate, $M_i$ is the associated ion momentum quantity for the ion population under consideration, and $S_{M_i}^{(\gamma)}$ is the corresponding proportional contribution to the ion momentum source term.

This quantity is the rate coefficient itself, not the ion momentum, the full source term, a force density, or a torque. The parent name does not select a spatial component, coordinate direction, flux-surface projection, explicit or implicit numerical treatment, isotope, or charge state; those distinctions require more specific names.

The [implicit ion momentum source rate](name:implicit_ion_momentum_source_rate) is an implicit-treatment specialization of this ion parent, used when the proportional source or sink contribution is represented implicitly. Source contributions that are not proportional to the associated ion momentum quantity are outside this rate-coefficient definition.

Sign convention: Positive when the proportional source term has the same sign as, or acts in the same direction as, the associated ion momentum quantity.

items.name: neutral_state_particle_diffusivity
items.description: Effective Fickian transport coefficient relating neutral-state particle flux to neutral-state number-density gradients, with directional components represented by more specific quantities.
items.documentation:
Neutral-state particle diffusivity is the effective transport coefficient for particle spreading driven by a neutral-state number-density gradient. It is the neutral-charge-state specialization of [particle diffusivity](name:particle_diffusivity), with directional components represented by more specific quantities.

For each resolved direction $i$, the diffusive particle flux of neutral state $\alpha$ is defined by

$$
\Gamma_{\alpha,i}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -D_{\alpha,i}\,\frac{\partial n_\alpha}{\partial x_i}
$$

where $\Gamma_{\alpha,i}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the diffusive particle flux of neutral state $\alpha$ along resolved transport direction $i$, $D_{\alpha,i}$ is the corresponding neutral-state particle diffusivity component, $n_\alpha$ is the number density of that neutral state, and $x_i$ is the coordinate along the resolved transport direction. The minus sign defines down-gradient diffusive transport for a positive coefficient.

This parent quantity selects a specified neutral state and does not aggregate over different neutral states, but it does not specify a transport direction or microscopic mechanism. Direction-specific instances include [poloidal neutral-state particle diffusivity](name:poloidal_neutral_state_particle_diffusivity).

items.name: ion_state_particle_flux_limiter_coefficient
items.description: Dimensionless particle flux-limiter coefficient for ions in a specified charge state that scales the admissible particle flux relative to its collisionless free-streaming bound.
items.documentation:
The dimensionless particle flux-limiter coefficient for an ion in a specified charge state controls the admissible particle flux in the density equation by scaling its collisionless free-streaming bound. It applies to the thermal and nonthermal particle populations represented by that ion state.

The limiting relation is

$$
\Gamma_{\mathrm{lim}} = \alpha_{p}\,\Gamma_{\mathrm{fs}}
$$

where $\Gamma_{\mathrm{lim}}$ is the limited particle flux for the selected ion state, $\alpha_{p}$ is this particle flux-limiter coefficient, and $\Gamma_{\mathrm{fs}}$ is the corresponding collisionless free-streaming particle-flux bound.

The coefficient is resolved for one specified ion charge state and is not summed over ion charge states. It applies to particle transport only, excluding the distinct energy- and momentum-flux limiter coefficients; it is also distinct from the [neutral-state particle flux-limiter coefficient](name:neutral_state_particle_flux_limiter_coefficient), which applies to a neutral internal state. The undirected coefficient is not a poloidal, parallel, or vertical projection.

This quantity is the ion-state specialization of the broader [particle flux-limiter coefficient](name:particle_flux_limiter_coefficient): the parent supplies the same particle-transport limiting concept without this ion-state restriction.

items.name: z_direction_unit_vector_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror
items.description: Signed component along the z axis of the unit vector defining an electron-cyclotron launcher mirror's translation direction or rotation axis at its home position, in the right-handed Cartesian (x, y, z) frame.
items.documentation:
Signed component along the z axis of the unit vector defining an electron-cyclotron launcher mirror's translation direction or rotation axis at its home position is the scalar projection of that mirror direction vector onto the z-axis basis direction in the right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$ frame. The $\hat{z}$ basis direction is vertical.

For mirror direction unit vector $\mathbf{u}$, the component is defined by:

$$
u_z = \mathbf{u}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{z}}, \qquad \lVert\mathbf{u}\rVert = 1
$$

where $u_z$ is the z-axis component of the electron-cyclotron launcher mirror direction unit vector, $\mathbf{u}$ is the unit vector defining that mirror's translation direction or rotation axis at its home position, $\hat{\mathbf{z}}$ is the positive z-axis basis vector in the right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$ frame, and $\lVert\mathbf{u}\rVert$ is the Euclidean norm of $\mathbf{u}$.

The quantity applies to an individual electron-cyclotron launcher mirror at its home position. It is a single Cartesian component of the movement direction or rotation axis, not an aggregate over launchers or mirrors and not an average over a range of mirror motion.

It is not a mirror position, displacement, the vertical coordinate of a point, or the angle of the electron-cyclotron launcher mirror. The corresponding [x-axis component](name:x_direction_unit_vector_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror) and [y-axis component](name:y_direction_unit_vector_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror) complete the same home-position unit vector; with $u_x$ and $u_y$ denoting those linked components, the components satisfy $u_x^2 + u_y^2 + u_z^2 = 1$.

items.name: power_of_plant_subsystem
items.description: Real electrical power consumed by an individual plant subsystem at its electrical boundary, contributing to auxiliary-load accounting without including plant-wide aggregation.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the real electrical power consumed by one plant subsystem at its electrical boundary. It represents the subsystem's contribution to auxiliary electrical load, distinct from plant-wide aggregation and net electrical balance quantities.

$$
P_{\rm sub} = \left\langle v(t)i(t) \right\rangle_t
$$

where $P_{\rm sub}$ is the boundary real power, $v(t)$ is the instantaneous terminal voltage, $i(t)$ is the instantaneous current directed into the subsystem, and $\langle\cdot\rangle_t$ denotes averaging over the relevant operating interval. For multiple terminals, the boundary power is the algebraic sum of the terminal power contributions. Positive power denotes consumption by the subsystem; exported or generated power is not included as consumed load. The quantity is distinct from absorbed power of a plant system, total power of a plant system, and net power of a plant system.

items.name: coolant_pressure
items.description: Absolute static pressure of the coolant or working fluid at a plant-system component port, referenced to perfect vacuum rather than atmospheric or another gage reference.
items.documentation:
The quantity is the local thermodynamic pressure of the coolant or working fluid at a component-port interface, with perfect vacuum as the zero-pressure reference. Static pressure is the isotropic mechanical stress of the fluid and excludes kinetic-energy contributions associated with bulk flow.

$$
\boldsymbol{\sigma}=-p_{\mathrm{abs}}\mathbf{I}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\sigma}$ is the isotropic fluid Cauchy stress, $p_{\mathrm{abs}}$ is the absolute static pressure, and $\mathbf{I}$ is the identity tensor.

The value represents local pressure at the port, not stagnation pressure, pressure drop, or pressure difference. At a cooling-circuit inlet, it is related to cooling-circuit inlet pressure, while coolant flow through a plant component port describes mass transport rather than mechanical pressure.

items.name: parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_source
items.description: Parallel ion charge-state momentum source is the parallel projection of the area-normalized momentum source acting on one specified ion charge state. It represents momentum transfer along the local magnetic-field direction.
items.documentation:
Parallel ion charge-state momentum source is the parallel projection of the area-normalized momentum source acting on one specified ion charge state. It represents directional momentum transfer to or from that charge state resolved along the local magnetic-field direction, rather than summed over charge states.

The parallel projection is defined by projecting the momentum-source vector for that charge state onto the local magnetic-field unit vector:

$$
S_{\parallel,i,Z} = \mathbf{S}_{i,Z} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{b}}
$$

where $\mathbf{S}_{i,Z}$ is the area-normalized momentum-source vector acting on ion species $i$ in charge state $Z$, and $\hat{\mathbf{b}} = \mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$ is the unit vector along the local magnetic field.

This quantity is distinct from the [poloidal ion charge-state momentum source](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_source) and the [toroidal ion charge-state momentum source](name:toroidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_source), which use poloidal and toroidal projections of the same charge-state-resolved momentum source.

Sign convention: Positive when the momentum-source vector acting on the charge state has a component in the direction of $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$, the local magnetic-field unit vector.

items.name: toroidal_argon_velocity_at_pedestal_top
items.description: Toroidal argon velocity at the pedestal top is the φ component, in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, of the density-weighted mean bulk flow of argon impurity ions where the H-mode pedestal transitions to the confined core.
items.documentation:
Toroidal argon velocity at the pedestal top is the $\phi$ component, in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, of the density-weighted mean bulk flow of argon impurity ions where the H-mode pedestal transitions to the confined core. As an intensive species-level quantity, it is the density-weighted mean over all argon charge states, not a charge-state-summed velocity.

The charge-state aggregation is defined by the density-weighted mean at the pedestal top:

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{Ar}}^{\mathrm{ped}} = \frac{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{Ar}^{q+}}^{\mathrm{ped}} v_{\phi,\mathrm{Ar}^{q+}}^{\mathrm{ped}}}{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{Ar}^{q+}}^{\mathrm{ped}}}
$$

where $q$ indexes argon ionization state, $n_{\mathrm{Ar}^{q+}}^{\mathrm{ped}}$ is the local number density of that charge state, and $v_{\phi,\mathrm{Ar}^{q+}}^{\mathrm{ped}}$ is its toroidal velocity component at the pedestal top.

It is inferred primarily from Doppler spectroscopy of argon emission, often charge-exchange recombination spectroscopy when suitable neutral-beam excitation is available. The observed line shift and viewing geometry determine the velocity projected onto the $\hat{\phi}$ direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame; estimating the all-charge-state mean may require emissivity modeling, ionization-balance information, or collisional equilibration assumptions.

Because pedestal argon rotation is sensitive to external torque, radial electric-field shear, neoclassical friction, turbulence-driven momentum transport, and charge-state distribution, no device-independent numerical range is implied. This value is commonly interpreted with same-species values at other loci, including [toroidal argon velocity at the magnetic axis](name:toroidal_argon_velocity_at_magnetic_axis), [toroidal argon velocity at the internal transport barrier](name:toroidal_argon_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier), [toroidal argon velocity at the plasma boundary](name:toroidal_argon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary), and toroidal flux-surface-averaged argon velocity at the plasma boundary.

Sign convention: Positive when the density-weighted mean argon flow points in the $+\hat{\phi}$ direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: neon_source_rate
items.description: Instantaneous injection rate of neon gas into the plasma vessel, expressed as an equivalent-electron count rate with ten counts assigned to each injected neon atom.
items.documentation:
Instantaneous injection rate of neon gas into the plasma vessel is the time rate of increase of the equivalent-electron count associated with injected neon. The equivalent-electron convention assigns ten counts to each injected neon atom, reflecting neon's atomic number.

The defining relation to injected atom count is:

$$
S_\mathrm{Ne} = \frac{dN_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^\mathrm{Ne}}{dt} = 10\,\frac{dN_\mathrm{Ne}}{dt}
$$

where $S_\mathrm{Ne}$ is the neon source rate, $N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^\mathrm{Ne}$ is the equivalent-electron count assigned to injected neon, $N_\mathrm{Ne}$ is the count of injected neon atoms, $t$ is time, and the label $\mathrm{Ne}$ denotes neon.

This quantity is species-specific to neon gas entering the plasma vessel and is aggregated over the injected neon population by summing the equivalent-electron contributions from all injected neon atoms. It excludes injection of other gasses, total gas throughput, pumping or exhaust flow, retained neutral inventory, and source terms from wall recycling, sputtering, or ionization inside the plasma.

The corresponding [accumulated neon count](name:accumulated_neon_count) is the time integral of $S_\mathrm{Ne}$ over the accumulation interval using the same factor of ten. Conversely, where differentiable, $S_\mathrm{Ne}$ is the time derivative of that accumulated count.

Sign convention: Positive when neon is added to the plasma vessel.

items.name: parallel_total_current_density
items.description: Parallel total current density is the flux-surface average of the total current–magnetic-field dot product divided by the reference vacuum toroidal field.
items.documentation:
Parallel total current density represents the net field-aligned conventional charge flow using a magnetic-field-weighted flux-surface average and a reference vacuum toroidal field. It is the parallel-basis member of [total current density](name:total_current_density), rather than the full current-density vector.

The defining relation is:

$$
j_\parallel = \frac{\left\langle \mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{tot}}\cdot\mathbf{B}\right\rangle}{B_0}
$$

where $j_\parallel$ is the parallel total current density, $\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{tot}}$ is the net plasma [current-density vector](name:current_density), $\mathbf{B}$ is the local magnetic-field vector, angle brackets denote a normalized flux-surface average, and $B_0$ is the signed reference vacuum toroidal magnetic field at the specified reference major radius. The reference field must be nonzero.

The total is the algebraic sum over all included charged species and charge states. It includes ohmic current and non-inductive current, with bootstrap and externally driven currents included within the non-inductive contribution. Every contribution uses the same averaging and reference-field convention. This quantity is neither a current magnitude nor, in general, the local field-aligned projection or its unweighted flux-surface average.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. Unlike [vertical total current density](name:vertical_total_current_density), which resolves charge flow along the vertical direction, this quantity resolves the magnetic-field-aligned contribution; it is also distinct from the toroidal projection.

Sign convention: Positive when the flux-surface-averaged total current–magnetic-field dot product and $B_0$ have the same sign; $B_0$ is positive in the direction of increasing $\phi$.

items.name: parallel_ion_charge_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient
items.description: Fick's-law proportionality coefficient relating the density-normalized parallel diffusive thermal energy flux of a specified ion charge state to its local temperature gradient.
items.documentation:
The ion charge-state energy diffusion coefficient $D_{i,z,E,\parallel}$ quantifies gradient-driven diffusive transport of thermal energy carried by ions in one specified charge state $z$ along the magnetic field. It is the parallel component of the direction-agnostic [ion charge-state energy diffusion coefficient](name:ion_charge_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient).

The defining relation for the density-normalized parallel diffusive energy flux is:

$$
\frac{Q_{i,z,\parallel,\mathrm{diff}}}{n_{i,z}} = -D_{i,z,E,\parallel}\,\nabla_{\parallel} T_{i,z}
$$

where $Q_{i,z,\parallel,\mathrm{diff}}$ is the parallel diffusive thermal-energy flux of charge state $z$, $n_{i,z}$ is its number density, $T_{i,z}$ is its temperature, and $\nabla_{\parallel}$ is the derivative along the magnetic-field direction.

This coefficient applies to one specified ion charge state and is not summed over charge states. It excludes convective, advective, and $E \times B$ contributions; the broader [parallel ion energy diffusion coefficient](name:parallel_ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient) represents the corresponding transport aggregated over ion species.

items.name: net_efficiency_of_plant_system
items.description: Dimensionless ratio quantifying how effectively a plant system delivers signed net electrical power to an external load relative to the total internal electrical consumption needed to operate it.
items.documentation:
The net efficiency of a plant system is the dimensionless ratio of signed net electrical power exported outside the plant boundary to total internal electrical power consumed by plant systems over the same accounting interval. It is the net-electrical-gain specialization of [efficiency of a plant system](name:efficiency_of_plant_system), with recirculating electrical loads included in the net exported power balance.

The defining relation, including the corresponding net-power balance, is:

$$
\eta_{\mathrm{net,plant}} = \frac{P_{\mathrm{net}}}{P_{\mathrm{cons}}}, \qquad
P_{\mathrm{net}} = P_{\mathrm{gen}} - P_{\mathrm{int}}, \qquad
P_{\mathrm{cons}} = \sum_{i \in \mathcal{B}_{\mathrm{plant}}} P_{\mathrm{load},i}
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{net}}$ is the net electrical power of the plant system in W, $P_{\mathrm{cons}}$ is the positive total electrical consumption represented by [power of the plant system](name:power_of_plant_system) in W, $P_{\mathrm{gen}}$ is gross generated electrical power in W, $P_{\mathrm{int}}$ is the internal operational electrical consumption subtracted in the net-power balance in W, $P_{\mathrm{load},i}$ is the electrical consumption of included load $i$ in W, and $\mathcal{B}_{\mathrm{plant}}$ is the set of electrically powered plant loads included in the accounting boundary.

The denominator $P_{\mathrm{cons}}$ is a gross positive consumption quantity, not the signed net exchange $P_{\mathrm{net}}$ and not the gross generated power $P_{\mathrm{gen}}$. It equals the internal-consumption term $P_{\mathrm{int}}$ only when the same loads, plant boundary, and interval define both the net-power balance and the denominator. Unlike [thermal efficiency of the plant system](name:thermal_efficiency_of_plant_system), this quantity relates net electrical export to internal electrical consumption rather than gross electrical output to thermal input.

Sign convention: Positive when signed net electrical power is exported from the plant system to an external electrical network or load.

items.name: particle_density
items.description: Particle number density is the concentration of a selected species, including thermal and nonthermal particles and all orbit classes unless a narrower population is specified.
items.documentation:
Particle number density is the local concentration of particles belonging to a selected species or population. For the full species distribution, it includes both thermal and nonthermal particles and all orbit classes.

The local density is the zeroth velocity-space moment of the distribution function:

$$
n_s(\mathbf{x}) = \int f_s(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $s$ labels the selected species, $n_s$ is its local particle number density, $\mathbf{x}$ is physical position, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $f_s$ is its particle-number distribution in position and velocity space, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element.

The quantity refers to one selected species, not a sum over different species. For a species specified without charge-state resolution, its number density is summed over all charge states; a charge-state-resolved population retains only the selected state's contribution. The local value does not imply flux-surface averaging; a flux-surface-averaged form averages this same local moment over a magnetic flux surface.

The [fast-particle density](name:fast_particle_density) is the same moment restricted to suprathermal particles and excludes the thermal population. It contributes to, but is distinct from, the full species density. Distinct nonthermal populations of the same species contribute additively to that full density.

items.name: reference_phase
items.description: Reference phase is the signed angular offset that fixes the phase origin of a complex oscillatory perturbation relative to a chosen zero-phase reference.
items.documentation:
Reference phase is the signed angular offset that sets the phase origin for a complex oscillatory perturbation relative to a chosen zero-phase reference. It parameterizes a phase gage: changing it rotates the complex amplitude without changing invariant perturbation properties such as magnitude, growth rate, or eigenfunction shape.

A perturbation quantity $\tilde{q}$ whose zero-phase representation is $\tilde{q}_0$ is shifted by the reference phase $\alpha$ as:

$$
\tilde{q} = \tilde{q}_0 \exp(i\alpha)
$$

where $\alpha$ is the reference phase and $\tilde{q}_0$ is the complex perturbation at the chosen zero-phase reference.

This parent quantity covers reference phases that choose the complex phase origin of perturbations, including the [mode reference phase](name:mode_reference_phase). It is not a physical propagation phase, a geometric position angle, or a phase difference between two independent signals unless that phase difference specifically defines the chosen reference offset.

Sign convention: Positive when the applied phase factor advances the perturbation by increasing its complex argument relative to the zero-phase reference.

items.name: parallel_neutral_species_particle_diffusivity
items.description: Effective particle diffusivity for an ion species along the magnetic field, relating its diffusive particle flux to its parallel number-density gradient.
items.documentation:
Effective parallel particle diffusivity for an ion species is the directional transport coefficient that represents ion-particle spreading driven by that species' number-density gradient. It is the field-parallel specialization of [ion particle diffusivity](name:ion_particle_diffusivity), with transport resolved along the magnetic field.

For the field-parallel direction, the diffusive ion-particle flux is defined by

$$
\Gamma_{\parallel,i}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -D_{\parallel,i}\frac{\partial n_i}{\partial s_{\parallel}}
$$

where $i$ identifies the selected ion species, $\Gamma_{\parallel,i}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is its parallel diffusive particle flux, $D_{\parallel,i}$ is its parallel particle diffusivity, $n_i$ is its ion number density, and $s_{\parallel}$ is physical arclength along the magnetic-field direction. The minus sign specifies down-gradient transport for positive diffusivity.

The density and diffusive flux are summed over all ionic charge states of the selected species, excluding neutral particles. This ion-species scope differs from [neutral-species particle diffusivity](name:neutral_species_particle_diffusivity) and its field-parallel counterpart, [parallel neutral particle diffusivity](name:parallel_neutral_particle_diffusivity). The coefficient describes particle diffusion only; it excludes convective particle flux and is distinct from energy and momentum diffusion coefficients.

items.name: etendue_of_bolometer
items.description: Geometric optical throughput of a bolometer channel, equal to the product of its effective collecting area and accepted solid angle.
items.documentation:
Étendue is the geometric optical throughput of a bolometer channel: the phase-space acceptance of rays transmitted from the viewed region to the detector. It determines how radiance is converted into collected optical power.

For a uniform angular acceptance, the étendue is defined by

$$
G = A\Omega
$$

where $G$ is the étendue, $A$ is the effective collecting area, and $\Omega$ is the accepted solid angle. For nonuniform acceptance, $G$ denotes the corresponding integral over the projected collecting area and accepted directions.

The quantity describes optical throughput only; detector conversion efficiency and electronic response are separate properties. It is the channel-level counterpart of [line-of-sight étendue](name:etendue_of_line_of_sight) and is closely related to the aperture area defined by [diagnostic aperture area](name:area_of_diagnostic_aperture).

items.name: radial_particle_convection_velocity
items.description: Signed major-radius component of the effective velocity multiplying neutral energy density in the convective energy flux of the edge plasma.
items.documentation:
Radial neutral-energy convection velocity is the effective coefficient of the energy-density-proportional advective flux carried by neutral particles in edge-plasma transport. It represents directed energy transport after the diffusive contribution has been separated.

The radial convective neutral-energy flux is defined by

$$
F_{E,n,R}^{\mathrm{conv}} = U_n v_{E,n,R}
$$

where $F_{E,n,R}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is the radial neutral-energy flux due to convection, $U_n$ is the energy density of the specified neutral population, and $v_{E,n,R}$ is this radial convection velocity.

The quantity applies to the neutral-energy channel, not the total-ion-energy channel or a sum over charged-particle energy channels. Its direction is the major-radius direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. This direction is not generally normal to a magnetic flux surface.

The quantity excludes diffusive energy transport and need not equal the bulk neutral flow velocity. It is distinct from the [neutral particle convection velocity](name:neutral_particle_convection_velocity), which multiplies neutral number density to define a convective particle flux; the energy-channel and particle-channel coefficients need not coincide.

Sign convention: Positive when the neutral-energy convection velocity points toward increasing major radius $R$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: trapped_current_density
items.description: Trapped current density is the vector density of conventional electric charge flux associated with trapped-particle transport, including its collisional drag back-current.
items.documentation:
Trapped current density is the vector density of conventional electric charge flux associated with the trapped-particle contribution. It includes direct charge transport by trapped particles and the collisional drag back-current attributed to that contribution.

A kinetic decomposition is

$$
\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{tr}}(\mathbf{x},t)=\sum_s q_s\int_{\mathcal{T}_s}\mathbf{v}\,f_s(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3v+\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{drag,tr}}(\mathbf{x},t)
$$

where $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $t$ is time, $s$ indexes charged species, $q_s$ is species charge, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $f_s$ is the velocity-space distribution function, $\mathcal{T}_s$ is the trapped-particle region of velocity space, and $\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{drag,tr}}$ is the associated collisional drag back-current.

This vector contribution is a specialization of [current_density](name:current_density), not a scalar electric current or a particular geometric projection. toroidal_current_density supplies a geometric projection, while [toroidal_trapped_current_density](name:toroidal_trapped_current_density) is the toroidal, flux-surface-averaged specialization of the trapped contribution.

Sign convention: Positive when any stated component or scalar projection of $\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{tr}}$ is aligned with the positive direction of its defining basis vector or unit vector.

items.name: source_rate_due_to_gas_injection
items.description: Instantaneous equivalent-electron source rate delivered to the plasma vessel by gas injection systems, where each injected atom contributes Z equivalent electrons per second according to its atomic number.
items.documentation:
The source rate due to gas injection characterizes the instantaneous rate at which neutral gas is admitted to the plasma vessel by gas injection hardware, expressed as an equivalent-electron count rate. Every injected atom of atomic number $Z$ contributes $Z$ equivalent electrons per second to the total inventory rate, providing a unified accounting framework across species of differing nuclear charge.

The defining relation for a single injected species is:

$$
\dot{S} = Z \cdot \dot{N}_{\mathrm{atoms}}
$$

where $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{atoms}}$ is the raw atomic delivery rate in atoms per second and $Z$ is the atomic number of the injected species. For simultaneous multi-species injection, contributions are summed over all active species.

This rate is inferred from calibrated mass-flow controllers or upstream pressure-rise measurements on the gas supply plumbing. It is the instantaneous time derivative of the corresponding accumulated equivalent-electron inventories, such as [accumulated_argon_count](name:accumulated_argon_count) or accumulated_hydrogen_count_due_to_gas_injection. The nearest-peer quantity gas_particle_source_rate_over_vessel_due_to_gas_injection provides the vessel-integrated analog expressed in raw gas-phase particles rather than equivalent electrons.

items.name: volume_averaged_neutral_species_density
items.description: Mean number density of a specified neutral species over the plasma volume enclosed by the last closed flux surface during plasma initiation.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the spatial mean of the local number density of one specified neutral species within the plasma volume enclosed by the last closed flux surface during plasma initiation. The local quantity is distinguished from [neutral_density](name:neutral_density), which is evaluated at a point.

$$
\overline{n}_0 = \frac{1}{V_{\mathrm{LCFS}}} \int_{V_{\mathrm{LCFS}}} n_0(\mathbf{r})\,dV
$$

where $n_0(\mathbf{r})$ is the local number density of the specified neutral species at position $\mathbf{r}$, $V_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$ is the volume enclosed by the last closed flux surface, and $dV$ is the volume element.

The average is species-specific and excludes neutral particles outside the enclosed volume. It is not the charge-state or population aggregate represented by [total_neutral_density](name:total_neutral_number_density), nor the volume average of ion density represented by [volume_averaged_ion_density](name:volume_averaged_ion_density).

items.name: magnetic_flux
items.description: Magnetic flux is the signed scalar surface integral of the magnetic field through an oriented surface. Its sign is set by the chosen surface orientation, while specializations identify the particular surface, field contribution, or averaging convention.
items.documentation:
Magnetic flux is a signed scalar associated with an oriented surface. It represents the net normal component of the magnetic field threading that surface; the flux itself is not a vector and is not directed, although its sign depends on the surface orientation.

The magnetic flux $\Phi$ through an oriented surface $S$ is defined by the surface integral:

$$
\Phi(S) = \int_S \mathbf{B} \cdot d\mathbf{A}
$$

where $\Phi(S)$ is the magnetic flux through $S$, $S$ is the oriented surface, $\mathbf{B}$ is the [magnetic-field vector](name:magnetic_field), $d\mathbf{A}=\hat{\mathbf{n}}\,dA$ is the oriented area element, $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ is the chosen unit normal to $S$, and $dA$ is the scalar surface-area element.

The unqualified quantity denotes the net integral over the specified oriented surface with no source restriction and no averaging. More specific flux quantities supply the surface family, source contribution, projection, or weighting that narrows this definition.

Magnetic flux is distinct from the local magnetic field, from a magnetic-field component or magnitude, from a flux-coordinate label normalized from a flux, and from a time derivative such as loop voltage. [Poloidal magnetic flux](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux) and [toroidal magnetic flux](name:toroidal_magnetic_flux) are specializations obtained by choosing different surfaces and orientations for the same integral; source-restricted or weighted quantities, such as [poloidal-current-weighted average external magnetic flux](name:poloidal_current_weighted_average_external_magnetic_flux), retain the magnetic-flux meaning while restricting the included magnetic field or applying the stated averaging convention.

Sign convention: Positive when the net magnetic-field projection through the specified surface is along the chosen orientation of its area element.

items.name: counter_passing_thermal_electron_power_density_due_to_collisions
items.description: Flux-surface-averaged rate of Coulomb-collisional energy transfer per unit volume from counter-passing nonthermal particles to bulk thermal electrons.
items.documentation:
Counter-passing thermal-electron collisional power density is the signed volumetric rate of kinetic-energy transfer from counter-passing nonthermal particles to bulk thermal electrons, averaged over a magnetic flux surface. Counter-passing particles follow untrapped guiding-center trajectories whose transit is opposite to the reference co-passing direction.

The transfer is defined by the thermal-electron kinetic-energy moment of the Coulomb collision operator:

$$
P_{e,\mathrm{counter}}^{\mathrm{coll}}(\psi) = \left\langle \sum_a \int \frac{1}{2}m_e v^2 C_{ea}[f_e^{\mathrm{th}},f_{a,\mathrm{counter}}] \, d^3v \right\rangle_\psi
$$

where $P_{e,\mathrm{counter}}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the flux-surface-averaged power density transferred to thermal electrons, $\psi$ labels the magnetic flux surface, $a$ indexes the represented nonthermal donor species, $m_e$ is the electron mass, $\mathbf{v}$ is electron velocity, and $v=|\mathbf{v}|$ is electron speed.
