The distribution $f_e^{\mathrm{th}}$ describes bulk thermal electrons, $f_{a,\mathrm{counter}}$ is the counter-passing part of the nonthermal distribution of species $a$, and $C_{ea}$ gives the collisional time derivative of the thermal-electron distribution caused by that donor population. The integral covers all electron velocities; the angle brackets denote the physical-volume-weighted average over an infinitesimal shell between neighboring flux surfaces.

The orbit restriction applies to the nonthermal donors, not to the receiving thermal electrons. The donor contributions are summed over the represented nonthermal species. Energy transferred to ions or fast electrons, contributions from co-passing or trapped donors, and noncollisional heating are excluded. This quantity describes energy gained by thermal electrons rather than energy gained by the counter-passing donors; the corresponding donor energy exchange has the opposite sign.

After applying the same flux-surface average to each contribution, adding the [co-passing thermal-electron contribution](name:co_passing_thermal_electron_power_density_due_to_collisions) and the [trapped thermal-electron contribution](name:trapped_thermal_electron_power_density_due_to_collisions) recovers the flux-surface average of [thermal-electron collisional power density](name:thermal_electron_power_density_due_to_collisions), which includes all represented donor orbit classes.

Sign convention: Positive when Coulomb collisions with counter-passing nonthermal particles transfer net kinetic energy to bulk thermal electrons.

items.name: toroidal_neutral_momentum_source
items.description: Toroidal component of the area-normalized momentum source for the neutral population in the edge plasma, summed over all neutral states. Its sign distinguishes neutral momentum transfer along increasing versus decreasing toroidal angle in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
The toroidal component of the area-normalized momentum source for the neutral population in the edge plasma, summed over all neutral states, is the net neutral momentum transfer per unit area resolved along the toroidal direction. It is one component of the aggregate [neutral momentum source](name:neutral_momentum_source) acting in the neutral momentum balance.

The toroidal component is defined by projecting the parent source vector onto the toroidal unit vector:

$$
S_{\phi,n} = \boldsymbol{S}_n \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $S_{\phi,n}$ is the toroidal neutral momentum source, $\boldsymbol{S}_n$ is the area-normalized [neutral momentum source](name:neutral_momentum_source) vector, and $\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. Here $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The quantity is summed over all neutral states and excludes ion momentum sources. Unlike the [radial neutral momentum source](name:radial_neutral_momentum_source), [poloidal neutral momentum source](name:poloidal_neutral_momentum_source), and [parallel neutral momentum source](name:parallel_neutral_momentum_source), it resolves momentum transfer along the toroidal direction rather than along major radius, the local poloidal direction, or the local magnetic-field direction.

Sign convention: Positive when the neutral momentum source points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: accumulated_krypton_count
items.description: Cumulative number of krypton atoms injected into the machine since plasma breakdown, expressed as 36 equivalent electrons for each krypton atom.
items.documentation:
Cumulative number of krypton atoms injected into the machine since plasma breakdown, expressed as 36 equivalent electrons for each krypton atom, is the post-breakdown time integral of the krypton atom influx into the machine with a fixed species multiplier. The multiplier is the krypton atomic number used as an equivalent-electron counting convention.

The accumulated count at time $t$ is defined by

$$
N_{\mathrm{Kr,acc}}(t) = Z_{\mathrm{Kr}} \int_{t_{\mathrm{bd}}}^{t} \dot{N}_{\mathrm{Kr}}(t')\,dt'
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{Kr,acc}}$ is the accumulated krypton count, $Z_{\mathrm{Kr}}=36$ is the krypton atomic-number multiplier, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Kr}}$ is the krypton atom injection rate into the machine, $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ is the plasma-breakdown time, $t$ is the evaluation time, and $t'$ is the integration time.

The scope is krypton introduced after plasma breakdown; it excludes krypton present before breakdown, non-krypton species, instantaneous injection rate, and any plasma number density. The species population is not charge-state resolved; if charge-state labels are used, krypton contributions are summed over all charge states before applying the fixed multiplier.

The equivalent-electron convention means this quantity equals 36 times the unweighted accumulated krypton atom count. It follows the same post-breakdown accumulated-species convention as [accumulated neon count](name:accumulated_neon_count), [accumulated ammonia count](name:accumulated_ammonia_count), and [accumulated helium-3 count due to gas injection](name:accumulated_helium_3_count_due_to_gas_injection). The factor 36 is a counting convention and does not specify the ionization state of the injected krypton.

items.name: poloidal_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift
items.description: Signed poloidal projection of the E×B guiding-center drift for one ion charge state in the edge plasma, along a specified local poloidal direction.
items.documentation:
The poloidal component of the [ion charge-state E×B drift velocity](name:ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift) is its signed projection along a specified local poloidal direction. This direction lies in the meridional plane of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is distance from the toroidal symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height; its positive orientation must be specified.

For the ideal E×B guiding-center drift, the defining projection is

$$
v_{E,\mathrm{p}} = \mathbf{v}_E \cdot \hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\mathrm{p}} = \frac{(\mathbf{E}\times\mathbf{B})\cdot\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\mathrm{p}}}{|\mathbf{B}|^2}.
$$

Here $v_{E,\mathrm{p}}$ is the poloidal drift component for the specified ion charge state, $\mathbf{v}_E$ is its ideal E×B drift velocity, $\mathbf{E}$ is the local electric field, $\mathbf{B}$ is the local magnetic field, and $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\mathrm{p}}$ is the unit vector along the specified positive local poloidal direction. The definition requires a nonzero magnetic field and magnetized ions.

This quantity applies locally to one specified charge state of one ion species in the edge plasma; it is neither summed nor averaged over charge states or species. At fixed local fields, the ideal drift is independent of ion mass and charge. Other contributions to the ion fluid velocity are excluded. It is a linear velocity component, not a poloidal angle or angular velocity.

Unlike the [parallel component](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift), which vanishes identically for the ideal E×B drift, the poloidal projection need not vanish: the local poloidal direction is not generally aligned with the magnetic field.

Sign convention: Positive when the E×B drift has a component along the specified positive local poloidal unit vector $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\mathrm{p}}$.

items.name: parallel_fast_particle_pressure
items.description: Parallel fast-particle pressure measures the field-aligned kinetic stress of a specified suprathermal population, including random and directed particle motion.
items.documentation:
The parallel fast-particle pressure is the field-aligned component of the kinetic stress carried by a specified suprathermal particle distribution. Together with the perpendicular component, it characterizes pressure anisotropy relative to the local magnetic field.

For a nonrelativistic species, the defining second velocity moment is:

$$
p_{\parallel,s,\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x}) = m_s \int v_\parallel^2 f_{s,\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $p_{\parallel,s,\mathrm{fast}}$ is the parallel fast-particle pressure of species $s$, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $m_s$ is the particle mass, $f_{s,\mathrm{fast}}$ is the fast-particle distribution function, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element. The parallel velocity is $v_\parallel=\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{b}$, where $\hat{b}=\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$ is the unit vector along the local magnetic field $\mathbf{B}$.

Only the suprathermal population represented by the specified distribution contributes; thermal-particle pressure is excluded. The quantity is not restricted to ions and does not imply an all-species or all-charge-state total. The velocity moment is not centered on the fast-particle mean flow, so directed parallel motion contributes in addition to random motion.

For the same population and spatial averaging, the [fast-particle pressure](name:fast_particle_pressure) is the trace pressure $p_{s,\mathrm{fast}}=(p_{\parallel,s,\mathrm{fast}}+2p_{\perp,s,\mathrm{fast}})/3$, where $p_{s,\mathrm{fast}}$ denotes the isotropic trace pressure and $p_{\perp,s,\mathrm{fast}}$ denotes the [perpendicular fast-particle pressure](name:perpendicular_fast_particle_pressure), the transverse kinetic stress per perpendicular degree of freedom. Parallel and perpendicular pressures need not be equal.

items.name: toroidal_neon_velocity_at_pedestal_top
items.description: Toroidal component of the density-weighted neon-ion fluid velocity at the core-side top of the H-mode edge transport barrier.
items.documentation:
Toroidal neon-ion velocity at the H-mode pedestal top is the density-weighted mean of the toroidal fluid velocities of all represented neon ion charge states at the core-side shoulder of the edge transport barrier. It is a signed projection in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

$$
V_{\mathrm{Ne},\phi} = \frac{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{Ne},q} v_{\mathrm{Ne},q,\phi}}{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{Ne},q}}
$$

Here, $q$ labels neon ion charge state, $n_{\mathrm{Ne},q}$ is its number density, and $v_{\mathrm{Ne},q,\phi}$ is its toroidal fluid-velocity component. The quantity is distinguished from [toroidal neon velocity at the internal transport barrier](name:toroidal_neon_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier) by its pedestal-top location and is a species-specific counterpart of [toroidal hydrogen velocity at the pedestal top](name:toroidal_hydrogen_velocity_at_pedestal_top).

Sign convention: Positive when the neon-ion flow has a component in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: inner_hard_xray_half_width_at_emissivity_peak
items.description: Dimensionless inward extent of the hard X-ray emissivity peak from its maximum to the inner half-maximum point in normalized toroidal flux.
items.documentation:
The inner half-width is the inward extent of the hard X-ray emissivity peak produced by fast electrons, measured along the normalized toroidal flux coordinate. It is the distance from the peak maximum toward the magnetic axis to the point where the emissivity falls to half its peak value.

$$
w_{\mathrm{in}} = \rho_{\mathrm{peak}} - \rho_{\mathrm{half,in}}, \qquad \varepsilon_X(\rho_{\mathrm{half,in}}) = \frac{1}{2}\varepsilon_X(\rho_{\mathrm{peak}})
$$

where $w_{\mathrm{in}}$ is the inner half-width, $\rho$ is the normalized toroidal flux coordinate increasing outward from the magnetic axis, and $\varepsilon_X(\rho)$ is the hard X-ray emissivity as a function of that coordinate. The subscript $\mathrm{peak}$ denotes the emissivity maximum, and $\mathrm{half,in}$ denotes the inward half-maximum location.

This quantity applies only to the side of the peak toward the magnetic axis. It is a geometric width, not an emissivity value, integrated emission, or average, and is distinct from the corresponding outward half-width. When both sides are defined, the full peak width is the sum of the inward and outward half-widths.

items.name: plasma_mass_density
items.description: Local plasma mass per unit volume, forming the inertial term in the MHD momentum equation and appearing in contexts from equilibrium transport profiles to linear MHD stability perturbations.
items.documentation:
The plasma mass density is the local plasma mass per unit volume, forming the inertial term in the MHD momentum balance and the compressibility term in the plasma continuity equation. This parent concept subsumes both equilibrium-profile and linear-perturbation contexts: the equilibrium total value summed over all charged species, and the complex first-order perturbation amplitude used in linear MHD eigenvalue problems.

In the equilibrium formulation, the mass density is defined by:

$$
\rho = \sum_s m_s n_s
$$

where $m_s$ is the particle mass and $n_s$ the number density of charged species $s$, summed over electrons, main-ion isotopes, and impurity charge states; neutral atoms are excluded. Ion contributions dominate because $m_i \gg m_e$.

In deuterium-dominated fusion plasmas at core electron densities of order $10^{20}$ m$^{-3}$, the mass density is approximately $3 \times 10^{-7}$ kg m$^{-3}$, scaling directly with ion density and average ion mass. The mass density sets the local Alfvén speed $v_A = B / \sqrt{\mu_0 \rho}$, where $B$ is the local magnetic-field magnitude and $\mu_0$ is the permeability of free space, governing the [alfven_time](name:alfven_time) and ideal-MHD wave dynamics. It enters inertial_current_density through the plasma-fluid acceleration term and is inferred from electron_number_density measurements combined with plasma composition analysis. This quantity is closely related to [mass_density](name:total_plasma_mass_density), which covers the same physical concept without explicit species qualification.

items.name: toroidal_implicit_ion_momentum_source_rate
items.description: Toroidal implicit ion momentum source rate is the signed coefficient multiplying one ion species’ toroidal momentum, with negative values describing proportional damping.
items.documentation:
Toroidal implicit ion momentum source rate is the coefficient of the proportional source contribution treated implicitly in an ion species’ toroidal momentum equation. It is the toroidal specialization of [implicit ion momentum source rate](name:implicit_ion_momentum_source_rate), rather than a dimensional momentum source.

Its defining relation is:

$$
\left(\frac{\partial P_{i,\phi}}{\partial t}\right)_{\mathrm{imp}} = S_{i,\phi}^{\mathrm{imp}} P_{i,\phi}
$$

where $P_{i,\phi}$ is the primary toroidal [momentum](name:momentum) quantity for ion species $i$, $t$ is time, $S_{i,\phi}^{\mathrm{imp}}$ is this source coefficient, and the label $\mathrm{imp}$ identifies the implicitly treated source contribution. The toroidal direction is the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius and $Z$ is vertical height.

The coefficient applies to one specified ion species, with the primary momentum summed over that species’ ionic charge states. It is neither summed over all ion species nor explicitly charge-state resolved; the coefficient itself is not a sum of charge-state coefficients.

Unlike a positive [momentum damping rate](name:momentum_damping_rate), this signed coefficient can describe either proportional amplification or damping. It excludes the additive source contribution independent of the primary momentum and is not a volume-integrated torque such as [toroidal explicit ion torque](name:toroidal_explicit_ion_torque).

Sign convention: Positive when the implicit source contribution reinforces the existing toroidal momentum; negative when it opposes that momentum and damps its magnitude.

items.name: accumulated_hydrogen_prefill_count
items.description: Cumulative equivalent-electron inventory of hydrogen atoms introduced by gas injection during prefill before plasma breakdown; hydrogen contributes one count per atom.
items.documentation:
The quantity is the cumulative hydrogen atom inventory delivered by gas injection during the prefill interval ending at plasma breakdown, expressed using the equivalent-electron convention. It is the hydrogen-specific contribution to the hydrogen prefill count.

$$
N_{\mathrm{H,eq}} = Z_{\mathrm{H}}N_{\mathrm{H}} = N_{\mathrm{H}}, \qquad N_{\mathrm{H}} = \int_{t_0}^{t_{\mathrm{bd}}} \dot{N}_{\mathrm{H}}(t)\,dt
$$

Here $N_{\mathrm{H,eq}}$ and $N_{\mathrm{H}}$ are dimensionless equivalent-electron and atom counts, $Z_{\mathrm{H}}=1$ is hydrogen's atomic number, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{H}}$ is the hydrogen injection rate in s$^{-1}$, and $t_0$ and $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ are the prefill start and breakdown times in s. Only pre-breakdown gas injection is included; post-breakdown delivery is represented by [accumulated hydrogen count due to gas injection](name:accumulated_hydrogen_count_due_to_gas_injection).

items.name: toroidal_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift
items.description: Signed toroidal projection of the mass- and charge-independent E×B guiding-center drift of one ion charge state in the edge plasma.
items.documentation:
The toroidal component of the [ion charge-state E×B drift velocity](name:ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift) is its signed projection along the geometric toroidal direction. This direction follows increasing toroidal angle in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is distance from the toroidal symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

For the ideal E×B guiding-center drift, the defining projection is

$$
v_{E,\phi} = \mathbf{v}_E \cdot \hat{\phi} = \frac{(\mathbf{E}\times\mathbf{B})\cdot\hat{\phi}}{|\mathbf{B}|^2}.
$$

Here $v_{E,\phi}$ is the toroidal drift component for the specified ion charge state, $\mathbf{v}_E$ is its E×B guiding-center drift velocity, $\mathbf{E}$ is the local electric field, $\mathbf{B}$ is the local magnetic field with magnitude $|\mathbf{B}|$, and $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector toward increasing toroidal angle. The definition requires a nonzero magnetic field and the magnetized guiding-center regime. At fixed local fields, the ideal drift is independent of ion mass and charge.

This quantity applies locally to one specified charge state of one ion species in the edge plasma; it is neither summed nor averaged over charge states or species. Other contributions to ion motion are excluded. It is a linear velocity component, not a toroidal angle, angular velocity, or drift-speed magnitude.

Unlike the [parallel component](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift), which vanishes identically for the ideal E×B drift, the toroidal projection need not vanish: the geometric toroidal direction is not generally aligned with the local magnetic field.

Sign convention: Positive when the E×B drift velocity has a component in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.
